objects.description: Represents a single classification result: either a single Unicode character or a ligature expansion encoded in UTF‑8, stored inline in a fixed-size array. Provides utilities to access UTF‑8/UTF‑32, get the first code point, and iterate over a UTF‑8 byte sequence via a nested const_iterator. Construction is from a UTF‑8 string or a single UCS-4 code point. Memory is internal; utf8_str() allocates a terminated copy that the caller must delete[].

A forward iterator over a UTF‑8 byte sequence that yields UCS‑4 code points and provides access to the current code point’s UTF‑8 bytes. It does not own the underlying data and is constructed via UNICHAR::begin/end().
Enumerates strong script directionality classifications for text ranges: neutral, LTR, RTL, or mixed.

objects.definition: using UNICHAR_ID = int;
objects.description: Type alias for a unique identifier of a UNICHAR entry. It is an integer ID, distinct from the character data itself.

objects.definition: using char32 = signed int;
objects.description: Alias for a 32-bit signed integer used to hold Unicode code points (UCS-4).

Plain-old-data struct describing a single recognized character and its bounding box/formatting metadata in Tesseract OCR output. char_code bytes are emitted in UTF-8 and multi-byte UTF-8 code points are represented as multiple consecutive entries sharing the same bounding box. Missing positions may be -1 per comments. Confidence is 0 (best) to 100 (reject).

Header/descriptor for OCR output and progress reporting. Acts as a progress monitor during recognition and as the container for recognized character data. Contains callbacks for cancellation and progress, a deadline mechanism, and an inline flexible array member text[1] of EANYCODE_CHAR used as the start of a variable-length buffer. Users typically allocate enough memory to hold the header plus N characters and read count to know how many are valid.

objects.definition: using CANCEL_FUNC = bool (*)(void *, int);
objects.description: Function pointer type for a cancellation callback: given a user pointer and the number of user words found, returns true to cancel ongoing OCR.

objects.definition: using PROGRESS_FUNC = bool (*)(int, int, int, int, int);
objects.description: Function pointer type for a legacy progress callback. Parameters are (progress_percent, left, right, top, bottom). Return value typically indicates continue (true) or cancel (false).

objects.definition: using PROGRESS_FUNC2 = bool (*)(ETEXT_DESC *, int, int, int, int);
objects.description: Function pointer type for a monitor-aware progress callback. Receives the ETEXT_DESC instance and the bounding box (left, right, top, bottom). Return value typically indicates continue (true) or cancel (false).

Iterator over Tesseract's page layout hierarchy (blocks, paragraphs, lines, words, symbols) without exposing internal engine types. Provides navigation (Begin/Next/Restart*), position queries, geometric data (bounding boxes, baselines, row metrics), orientation/paragraph info, and image extraction for the current element. The iterator references PAGE_RES data owned by TessBaseAPI and is only valid while that data remains intact; it becomes invalid after operations like Init, SetImage, Recognize, Clear, End, etc. Bounding box behavior can include/exclude diacritic components via SetBoundingBoxComponents.

Bi-directional reading-order-aware iterator over Tesseract recognition results. Extends LTRResultIterator to correctly traverse paragraphs, lines, words, and symbols in mixed-direction scripts (e.g., Hebrew/English). Provides text extraction (UTF-8) and access to LSTM timestep and best-choice symbol data for the current word. Maintains internal state about paragraph direction and minor (opposite-direction) runs. Constructors are limited: creation is via static StartOfParagraph from an existing LTRResultIterator; copy construction uses the compiler default; destructor is virtual and defaulted.

Iterator over OCR results in strict left-to-right order, exposing text-specific accessors without requiring internal Tesseract data structures. It derives from PageIterator and provides text content, confidence, word attributes, and symbol attributes. Lifespan is tied to TessBaseAPI’s internal PAGE_RES; instances must not outlive or be used after API reinitialization/clearing. Construction requires PAGE_RES and Tesseract pointers plus image rectangle/scale metadata. Destruction is virtual via base. Details of ownership for PAGE_RES and Tesseract are external; this class does not own them.

One-shot iterator over classifier choices for the current RIL_SYMBOL indicated by an LTRResultIterator. Exposes choice text, confidence, and optional LSTM timestep distributions. Internally references WERD_RES and classifier choice iterators owned by the API; does not own them and becomes invalid once the associated LTRResultIterator/API state changes.

Abstract base class for rendering OCR results produced by TessBaseAPI into various output formats. Manages document lifecycle (BeginDocument, AddImage, EndDocument), output accumulation, and chaining of multiple renderers. Must be subclassed with an implementation of AddImageHandler; optional hooks exist for begin/end document handling. Owns output state and can be linked to other renderers via insert/next.
Concrete renderer writing OCR output as plain UTF-8 text. Constructed with an output base path; implements AddImageHandler to append recognized text for each image.
Renderer producing hOCR HTML-like output. Optional font_info flag controls inclusion of font data. Overrides begin/add/end handlers to manage hOCR document structure.
Renderer producing ALTO XML output. Manages document start/end state with begin_document flag and per-image content emission.
Renderer producing PAGE XML output. Tracks document lifecycle and emits PAGE-compliant structures for each image.
Renderer producing tab-separated value (TSV) output. Optional font_info flag includes font attributes. Overrides lifecycle handlers for TSV formatting.

Renderer producing searchable PDF files. Uses Tesseract data directory to load custom font; can operate in text-only mode. Manages PDF object bookkeeping and per-page content generation, including optional image transcoding.
Renderer producing UNLV plain-text style output. Implements per-image text emission via AddImageHandler.
Renderer producing UTF-8 text in LSTM box training format. Used for generating training data with bounding boxes from LSTM-based recognition.
Renderer producing plain UTF-8 text with bounding box annotations (box text format).
Renderer producing UTF-8 text in WordStr box format, a word-level string box representation used by some Tesseract tooling.
Renderer producing OSD (Orientation and Script Detection) text output. Available when legacy engine is enabled (not compiled with DISABLED_LEGACY_ENGINE).

objects.definition: struct Pix;
objects.description: Forward declaration of Pix image type (likely from Leptonica). Only referenced here; no definition provided in this header.

objects.definition: class TessBaseAPI;
objects.description: Forward declaration of the main Tesseract OCR API class used to perform recognition. Only referenced here; no definition provided in this header.

Best combined result of orientation and script estimation for a page or region. Holds the chosen orientation and script ids and their confidences. Constructed with zeros by default. No ownership or resource management semantics.

Aggregates orientation and script detection scores. Holds per-orientation scores, per-script scores for each orientation, a pointer to an associated UNICHARSET (not owned), and the current best result. Provides methods to update, set, accumulate, and print scores. Default constructor zero-initializes score arrays and sets unicharset to null.

Helper that estimates page orientation from per-blob script/character scores. It updates an OSResults instance using allowed script ids. It does not own the OSResults or allowed scripts pointers. Construction requires allowed script list and an OSResults to populate.

Detector that scores scripts for blobs and updates OSResults, with awareness of specific script ids (Korean, Japanese, etc.) and access to a Tesseract engine instance. Pointers to OSResults, Tesseract, and allowed scripts are not owned. Provides a stopping heuristic via must_stop.

Primary Tesseract OCR C++ API class. Manages initialization, image input, page layout analysis, recognition, and result export in various formats. Holds pointers to internal engines and state. Construct with TessBaseAPI(), call Init(), SetImage()/Recognize(), then retrieve text/iterators. Call End() to release resources.

objects.definition: using FileReader = bool (*)(const char *filename, std::vector<char> *data);
objects.description: Function pointer type for reading an entire file into a std::vector<char>. Returns false on failure.

objects.description: Pointer-to-member-function type of Dict to compute probability in context for strings. Set via TessBaseAPI::SetProbabilityInContextFunc.

Opaque handle to a Tesseract result renderer. In C builds this is an incomplete struct used as an opaque type; in C++ it aliases tesseract::TessResultRenderer. Used to render OCR results to various formats (text, hOCR, PDF, etc.).

Opaque handle to the main Tesseract OCR engine API object. In C builds this is an incomplete struct; in C++ it aliases tesseract::TessBaseAPI. Manages engine initialization, image input, recognition, and result retrieval.
Opaque iterator over page layout elements (blocks, paragraphs, lines, words, symbols).
Opaque iterator to traverse recognition results with access to text, confidence, and attributes.
Opaque iterator similar to ResultIterator but allows modifications to the result structure. Only referenced/returned; no constructors here.
Opaque iterator over alternative recognition choices for the current symbol/word.
Enumeration selecting the OCR engine(s) to use. In C builds it is defined here; in C++ it aliases tesseract::OcrEngineMode. Pointer form is rarely used but provided per spec.

Enumeration of page orientation values.
Enumeration for paragraph text justification.
Enumeration for dominant writing direction.
Enumeration for text line ordering on the page.

functions.name: tesseract::PTIsLineType
functions.description: Returns true if the given PolyBlockType represents a line element (horizontal or vertical line). Intended for quick classification of ColPartition/POLY_BLOCK types when deciding how to treat layout elements.
requirements: Argument type must be a valid tesseract::PolyBlockType value.
Returns true only for PT_HORZ_LINE and PT_VERT_LINE; false otherwise.
Pure function; has no side effects and is thread-safe.

functions.name: tesseract::PTIsImageType
functions.description: Returns true if the given PolyBlockType represents an image region (flowing, heading, or pullout image). Useful for filtering non-text partitions/blocks.
requirements: Argument type must be a valid tesseract::PolyBlockType value.
Returns true only for PT_FLOWING_IMAGE, PT_HEADING_IMAGE, or PT_PULLOUT_IMAGE; false otherwise.
Pure function; has no side effects and is thread-safe.

functions.name: tesseract::PTIsTextType
functions.description: Returns true if the given PolyBlockType represents a text region (flowing, heading, pullout text, table, vertical text, caption text, or inline equation).
requirements: Argument type must be a valid tesseract::PolyBlockType value.
Returns true only for PT_FLOWING_TEXT, PT_HEADING_TEXT, PT_PULLOUT_TEXT, PT_TABLE, PT_VERTICAL_TEXT, PT_CAPTION_TEXT, or PT_INLINE_EQUATION; false otherwise.
Pure function; has no side effects and is thread-safe.

functions.name: tesseract::PTIsPulloutType
functions.description: Returns true if the given PolyBlockType is an inter-column pullout region (pullout image or pullout text).
requirements: Argument type must be a valid tesseract::PolyBlockType value.
Returns true only for PT_PULLOUT_IMAGE or PT_PULLOUT_TEXT; false otherwise.
Pure function; has no side effects and is thread-safe.

functions.name: tesseract::PSM_OSD_ENABLED
functions.description: Indicates whether orientation and script detection (OSD) is enabled for the given page segmentation mode. Depends critically on the ordering of PageSegMode enum values.
requirements: pageseg_mode should correspond to a valid tesseract::PageSegMode value (0..PSM_COUNT-1).
Argument is int for compatibility; callers should pass values from PageSegMode to ensure meaningful results.
Returns true when pageseg_mode <= PSM_AUTO_OSD or == PSM_SPARSE_TEXT_OSD.
Pure function; has no side effects and is thread-safe.

functions.name: tesseract::PSM_ORIENTATION_ENABLED
functions.description: Indicates whether orientation detection is enabled for the given page segmentation mode. Relies on the defined order of PageSegMode values.
requirements: pageseg_mode should correspond to a valid tesseract::PageSegMode value (0..PSM_COUNT-1).
Argument is int for compatibility; callers should pass PageSegMode values.
Returns true when pageseg_mode <= PSM_AUTO or == PSM_SPARSE_TEXT_OSD.
Pure function; has no side effects and is thread-safe.

functions.name: tesseract::PSM_COL_FIND_ENABLED
functions.description: Returns true if column finding is enabled for the specified page segmentation mode. Ordering of PageSegMode is significant for this check.
requirements: pageseg_mode should correspond to a valid tesseract::PageSegMode value (0..PSM_COUNT-1).
Argument is int for compatibility; callers should pass PageSegMode values.
Returns true when PSM_AUTO_OSD <= pageseg_mode <= PSM_AUTO.
Pure function; has no side effects and is thread-safe.

functions.name: tesseract::PSM_SPARSE
functions.description: Returns true if the specified page segmentation mode is a sparse-text mode (no particular reading order, optionally with OSD).
requirements: pageseg_mode should correspond to a valid tesseract::PageSegMode value (0..PSM_COUNT-1).
Argument is int for compatibility; callers should pass PageSegMode values.
Returns true only for PSM_SPARSE_TEXT or PSM_SPARSE_TEXT_OSD.
Pure function; has no side effects and is thread-safe.

functions.name: tesseract::PSM_BLOCK_FIND_ENABLED
functions.description: Returns true if block finding is enabled for the specified page segmentation mode. Depends on the numeric order of PageSegMode.
requirements: pageseg_mode should correspond to a valid tesseract::PageSegMode value (0..PSM_COUNT-1).
Argument is int for compatibility; callers should pass PageSegMode values.
Returns true when PSM_AUTO_OSD <= pageseg_mode <= PSM_SINGLE_COLUMN.
Pure function; has no side effects and is thread-safe.

functions.name: tesseract::PSM_LINE_FIND_ENABLED
functions.description: Returns true if line finding is enabled for the specified page segmentation mode. Relies on the PageSegMode value ordering.
requirements: pageseg_mode should correspond to a valid tesseract::PageSegMode value (0..PSM_COUNT-1).
Argument is int for compatibility; callers should pass PageSegMode values.
Returns true when PSM_AUTO_OSD <= pageseg_mode <= PSM_SINGLE_BLOCK.
Pure function; has no side effects and is thread-safe.

functions.name: tesseract::PSM_WORD_FIND_ENABLED
functions.description: Returns true if word finding is enabled for the specified page segmentation mode. Uses ranges based on the ordered PageSegMode enum.
requirements: pageseg_mode should correspond to a valid tesseract::PageSegMode value (0..PSM_COUNT-1).
Argument is int for compatibility; callers should pass PageSegMode values.
Returns true when (PSM_AUTO_OSD <= pageseg_mode <= PSM_SINGLE_LINE) or pageseg_mode is PSM_SPARSE_TEXT or PSM_SPARSE_TEXT_OSD.
Pure function; has no side effects and is thread-safe.

functions.name: tesseract::UNICHAR::UNICHAR
functions.description: Constructs a UNICHAR from a UTF-8 byte sequence. If len < 0, utf8_str is treated as null-terminated. If the encoded string is longer than the internal storage allows, it stores only the leading bytes that fit.
requirements: utf8_str must point to a readable buffer; if len >= 0, the buffer must have at least len bytes accessible.
If len < 0, utf8_str must be null-terminated.
Only the first UNICHAR_LEN-1 bytes (effectively) may be stored; excess bytes are truncated (per comment: it takes only what will fit).
Input is expected to be UTF-8; behavior for invalid UTF-8 is not fully documented.

functions.name: tesseract::UNICHAR::UNICHAR
functions.description: Constructs a UNICHAR from a single UCS-4/Unicode code point.
requirements: unicode should be a valid Unicode scalar value; behavior for invalid values is not documented.
Creates exactly one code point worth of UTF-8 data inside the object.

functions.name: tesseract::UNICHAR::first_uni
functions.description: Returns the first character of the internal UTF-8 string as a UCS-4 code point.
requirements: The UNICHAR should contain at least one encoded character; behavior for empty/invalid internal data is not documented.

functions.name: tesseract::UNICHAR::utf8_len
functions.description: Returns the length in bytes of the stored UTF-8 string. Uses an internal length encoding; caps to [0, UNICHAR_LEN].
requirements: None beyond having a valid UNICHAR instance. Returned length may equal UNICHAR_LEN if internal length encoding is unavailable.

functions.name: tesseract::UNICHAR::utf8
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the internal UTF-8 byte array. The buffer is not null-terminated.
requirements: The returned pointer remains valid only as long as the UNICHAR object exists and is unmodified.
Callers must not assume a null terminator; use utf8_len() to know the byte count.
Do not modify the returned buffer.

functions.name: tesseract::UNICHAR::utf8_str
functions.description: Allocates and returns a null-terminated UTF-8 string containing the stored data. The caller must delete[] the returned buffer.
requirements: Caller must delete[] the returned pointer after use.
Returned string length equals utf8_len(); it is null-terminated.

functions.name: tesseract::UNICHAR::utf8_step
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes in the first UTF-8 code point at utf8_str.
requirements: utf8_str must point to at least one readable byte and enough bytes for the first code point; behavior on invalid/insufficient input is not documented.
Input is expected to be UTF-8 encoded.

functions.name: tesseract::UNICHAR::const_iterator::operator++
functions.description: Advances the iterator to the next UTF-8 code point. On an illegal UTF-8 byte sequence at the current position, it logs an error and advances by one byte. If currently at a null byte, it does not advance past it.
requirements: Underlying memory must remain valid for the iterator’s lifetime.
Caller should compare against an end iterator (from UNICHAR::end) to avoid stepping beyond the buffer.
Behavior includes error logging on illegal UTF-8; exact logging mechanism not specified.

functions.name: tesseract::UNICHAR::const_iterator::operator*
functions.description: Dereferences the iterator to return the UCS-4 code point at the current position. Returns a space character (U+0020) if the current position is at an illegal UTF-8 value.
requirements: Iterator must point within the bounds of the referenced buffer; dereferencing past the end is undefined.
On illegal UTF-8, returns space (per comment).

functions.name: tesseract::UNICHAR::const_iterator::get_utf8
functions.description: Writes the UTF-8 encoding of the current code point into buf and returns the number of bytes written. On illegal UTF-8 at the current position, writes a single space byte and returns 1. Does not null-terminate the buffer.
requirements: buf must point to a writable buffer of at least 4 bytes.
Iterator must be positioned at a code point within the referenced buffer.
Caller must add a null terminator if a C-string is required.

functions.name: tesseract::UNICHAR::const_iterator::utf8_len
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes of the current UTF-8 code point. Returns 1 if the current position is at an illegal UTF-8 value.
requirements: Iterator must point within the bounds of the referenced buffer.

functions.name: tesseract::UNICHAR::const_iterator::is_legal
functions.description: Returns true if the UTF-8 encoding at the current iterator position is a legal UTF-8 sequence; false otherwise.
requirements: Iterator must point within the bounds of the referenced buffer.

functions.name: tesseract::UNICHAR::const_iterator::utf8_data
functions.description: Returns the underlying pointer into the UTF-8 byte sequence at the iterator’s current position.
requirements: Returned pointer is valid only while the referenced buffer remains alive and unmodified.

functions.name: tesseract::UNICHAR::begin
functions.signature: static tesseract::UNICHAR::const_iterator tesseract::UNICHAR::begin(const char* utf8_str, int byte_length)
functions.description: Creates an iterator positioned at the start of a UTF-8 byte sequence. The iterator does not copy or take ownership of the underlying array.
requirements: utf8_str must point to a readable buffer of at least byte_length bytes.
The underlying buffer must outlive the iterator.
byte_length should be the number of valid bytes in utf8_str (may or may not include a trailing null).

functions.name: tesseract::UNICHAR::end
functions.signature: static tesseract::UNICHAR::const_iterator tesseract::UNICHAR::end(const char* utf8_str, int byte_length)
functions.description: Creates a past-the-end iterator corresponding to a UTF-8 byte sequence (pointer at utf8_str + byte_length). The iterator does not copy or take ownership of the array.
requirements: utf8_str must point to a readable buffer of at least byte_length bytes.
The underlying buffer must outlive the iterator.
Use together with begin() for range-style iteration and bounds checking.

functions.name: tesseract::UNICHAR::UTF8ToUTF32
functions.description: Converts a null-terminated UTF-8 string to a vector of UCS-4/UTF-32 code points. Returns an empty vector if the input contains invalid UTF-8.
requirements: utf8_str must be a null-terminated UTF-8 string.
On invalid UTF-8 anywhere in the input, the function returns an empty vector.

functions.name: tesseract::UNICHAR::UTF32ToUTF8
functions.description: Converts a vector of UCS-4/UTF-32 code points to a UTF-8 encoded std::string. Returns an empty string if the input contains an invalid Unicode value.
requirements: str32 elements should be valid Unicode scalar values; if any element is invalid, the function returns an empty string.

functions.name: tesseract::ETEXT_DESC::set_deadline_msecs
functions.description: Sets the internal deadline (end_time) to the current steady_clock time plus the specified number of milliseconds. Passing a positive value enables a deadline; zero or negative leaves the existing deadline unchanged. Typical usage: call this before starting a long operation to enforce a time limit that can later be checked with deadline_exceeded(). Notes: uses std::chrono::steady_clock for monotonic timing.
requirements: deadline_msecs must be greater than 0 to set or update the deadline; values <= 0 leave the deadline unchanged.
No other preconditions are stated; the method operates on the ETEXT_DESC instance’s internal end_time.

functions.name: tesseract::ETEXT_DESC::deadline_exceeded
functions.description: Returns true if the current steady_clock time is past the previously set deadline (end_time). If no deadline has been set (i.e., set_deadline_msecs was never called with a positive value), the function returns false. Typical usage: periodically poll during processing to decide whether to abort work due to timeout.
requirements: No preconditions to call. If no deadline has been set, the function will return false.
The determination is a strict comparison: it returns true only when now > end_time (not when equal).

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::PageIterator
functions.signature: tesseract::PageIterator::PageIterator(PAGE_RES *page_res, Tesseract *tesseract, int scale, int scaled_yres, int rect_left, int rect_top, int rect_width, int rect_height)
functions.description: Constructs a PageIterator bound to the current PAGE_RES and Tesseract engine from TessBaseAPI. Rectangle/scale parameters map iterator coordinates back to the original image coordinates. After construction, Begin() has already been called, so iteration starts at the beginning of the page.
requirements: page_res must point to a valid PAGE_RES owned by TessBaseAPI and remain valid for the iterator's lifetime.
tesseract must point to a valid Tesseract instance associated with page_res and remain valid while using the iterator.
The iterator may only be used while the owning TessBaseAPI remains alive and before any API calls that change PAGE_RES (Init, SetImage, Recognize, Clear, End, DetectOS, etc.).
scale must match the scale applied by the Thresholder; iterator image coordinates must be divided by scale before adding (rect_left, rect_top) to obtain original-image coordinates.
scaled_yres should reflect the effective resolution of the thresholded (binary) image.
rect_left, rect_top, rect_width, rect_height must correspond to the image rectangle set in TessBaseAPI (SetRectangle), using top-left-origin coordinates.

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::PageIterator
functions.description: Copy constructor. Creates a new PageIterator at the same position/state as src. Unlike the main constructor, this does not call Begin(), so iteration continues from src’s current location.
requirements: src must be a valid, initialized PageIterator whose underlying TessBaseAPI/PAGE_RES are still valid.
The new iterator shares pointers into API-owned data; the TessBaseAPI and PAGE_RES must remain valid while either iterator is in use.

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::~PageIterator
functions.description: Destructor for PageIterator. Releases any resources owned by the iterator. Does not own the PAGE_RES or Tesseract instances provided by the API.
requirements: The associated TessBaseAPI object should outlive the iterator or at least remain valid until the iterator is destroyed, as the iterator points into API-owned data.

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::operator=
functions.description: Assignment operator. Makes this iterator reference the same page and position as src without restarting the iteration.
requirements: src must be a valid PageIterator whose underlying TessBaseAPI/PAGE_RES are still valid.
After assignment, both iterators depend on the same API-owned PAGE_RES; TessBaseAPI and PAGE_RES must remain valid while either iterator is used.

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::PositionedAtSameWord
functions.description: Compares this iterator’s current position to another PAGE_RES iterator to determine if both point at the same word.
requirements: other must be a valid pointer to a PAGE_RES_IT positioned on the same PAGE_RES as this iterator.
Returns a boolean; caller should handle false when positions differ or when states are incomparable.

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::Begin
functions.description: Positions the iterator at the start of the page, beginning a fresh iteration over the page hierarchy.
requirements: Underlying PAGE_RES must be valid.
Subsequent navigation calls (Next/RestartRow/RestartParagraph) assume Begin() has been called unless you used a copy/assignment that preserves position.

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::RestartParagraph
functions.description: Moves the iterator to the beginning of the current paragraph. Implemented by moving to the zero-indexed blob of the first (leftmost) word on the first row of the paragraph.
requirements: Iterator must currently be positioned within a paragraph.
Underlying PAGE_RES must be valid; behavior is undefined at end-of-document.

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::IsWithinFirstTextlineOfParagraph
functions.description: Returns true if the current position lies within the first text line of the current paragraph; false otherwise.
requirements: Iterator must be validly positioned within the page; returns false if not within a first text line.

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::RestartRow
functions.description: Moves the iterator to the beginning of the current text line. Implemented by moving to the zero-indexed blob of the first (leftmost) word of the row.
requirements: Iterator must currently be positioned within a text line.
Underlying PAGE_RES must be valid.

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::Next
functions.description: Advances the iterator to the start of the next object at the specified level in the page hierarchy. Returns false if the end of the page is reached. RIL_SYMBOL skips non-text blocks; other levels will visit each non-text block once (treated as a single para/line/imaginary word). Supports correct iteration of right-to-left scripts if the appropriate language is loaded.
requirements: level must be a valid PageIteratorLevel enum value.

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::IsAtBeginningOf
functions.description: Returns true if the iterator is at the start of an object at the specified hierarchy level (e.g., beginning of a line, word, or symbol).
requirements: level must be a valid PageIteratorLevel enum value.
Iterator must be validly positioned; otherwise returns false.

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::IsAtFinalElement
functions.signature: virtual bool tesseract::PageIterator::IsAtFinalElement(PageIteratorLevel level, PageIteratorLevel element) const
functions.description: Returns true if the iterator is positioned at the last element of type ‘element’ within the containing ‘level’ object (e.g., last word in a line, last line in a block).
requirements: level and element must be valid PageIteratorLevel enum values.
Iterator must be validly positioned; otherwise returns false.

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::Cmp
functions.description: Compares this iterator’s position with another’s. Returns -1 if this is before other, 0 if equal, and 1 if after.
requirements: other must reference the same underlying document/PAGE_RES for meaningful comparison.
Caller must handle all three return values (-1, 0, 1).

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::SetBoundingBoxComponents
functions.description: Controls inclusion of potential diacritics (above/below dots) in bounding boxes for levels between RIL_WORD and RIL_BLOCK. Useful between layout analysis and recognition when diacritic ownership is uncertain.
requirements: include_upper_dots toggles inclusion of upper diacritics; include_lower_dots toggles inclusion of lower diacritics.
Affects BoundingBox/BoundingBoxInternal results for applicable levels.

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::BoundingBox
functions.signature: bool tesseract::PageIterator::BoundingBox(PageIteratorLevel level, int *left, int *top, int *right, int *bottom) const
functions.description: Returns the bounding rectangle of the current object at the given level, in the iterator’s coordinate system (see class comments). Returns false if no such object exists at the current position. The box matches the size/position of the image from GetBinaryImage and may clip some grayscale foreground pixels.
requirements: level must be a valid PageIteratorLevel.
left, top, right, bottom must be non-null pointers to receive coordinates.
Iterator must be validly positioned at an object of the requested level or the function returns false.
If an image rectangle was set in the API, the returned coordinates relate to the original (full) image.

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::BoundingBox
functions.signature: bool tesseract::PageIterator::BoundingBox(PageIteratorLevel level, int padding, int *left, int *top, int *right, int *bottom) const
functions.description: Like BoundingBox(level, ...), but allows specifying extra padding when computing the bounds, to better include foreground pixels that may be clipped in grayscale images.
requirements: level must be a valid PageIteratorLevel.
padding is an integer number of pixels to expand bounds (non-negative implied; exact constraints not specified).
left, top, right, bottom must be non-null pointers to receive coordinates.
Returns false if no object exists at the current position.

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::BoundingBoxInternal
functions.signature: bool tesseract::PageIterator::BoundingBoxInternal(PageIteratorLevel level, int *left, int *top, int *right, int *bottom) const
functions.description: Returns the bounding rectangle of the current object in the coordinate system of the working image rectangle whose origin is (rect_left_, rect_top_) relative to the original image and scaled by scale_.
requirements: level must be a valid PageIteratorLevel.
left, top, right, bottom must be non-null pointers to receive coordinates.
Returns false if no object exists at the current position.
Coordinates are in the scaled/offset working-rectangle system, not necessarily matching original image coordinates.

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::Empty
functions.description: Returns true if there is no object of the specified level at the current iterator position.
requirements: level must be a valid PageIteratorLevel.
Iterator must be validly positioned. Caller should handle true (empty) and false (non-empty).

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::BlockType
functions.description: Returns the PolyBlockType for the current block (e.g., text, image, table).
requirements: Iterator must be positioned within a block; otherwise the returned value may be unspecified.
PolyBlockType is defined in tesseract/publictypes.h; caller must interpret accordingly.

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::BlockPolygon
functions.description: Returns the polygon outline (as a Pta) of the current block. The Pta lists the vertices, with the last edge between the last point and the first. Returns nullptr at end of document or if layout analysis was not used.
requirements: Caller must free the returned Pta with ptaDestroy after use.
Iterator must be positioned within a block that has polygon data to receive a non-null result.

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::GetBinaryImage
functions.description: Returns a binary (1 bpp) image of the current object at the specified level. Its position and size match BoundingBoxInternal (and may be upscaled relative to the original input).
requirements: level must be a valid PageIteratorLevel.
Caller must free the returned Pix with pixDestroy after use.
Iterator must be positioned at a valid object of the given level; returns nullptr if not available (implied by typical API—exact nullability not explicitly stated).

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::GetImage
functions.signature: Pix *tesseract::PageIterator::GetImage(PageIteratorLevel level, int padding, Pix *original_img, int *left, int *top) const
functions.description: Returns an image of the current object at the given level in grayscale if available from the input; otherwise returns a binary image. Bounds are expanded by the specified padding to better include foreground pixels. The top-left of the returned image is provided via (left, top) and will likely not match BoundingBox coordinates.
requirements: level must be a valid PageIteratorLevel.
padding is an integer number of pixels for expansion (non-negative implied; exact constraints not specified).

left and top must be non-null pointers to receive the returned image origin.
Caller must free the returned Pix with pixDestroy after use.

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::Baseline
functions.signature: bool tesseract::PageIterator::Baseline(PageIteratorLevel level, int *x1, int *y1, int *x2, int *y2) const
functions.description: Returns the baseline of the current object at the specified level as a line through (x1,y1) and (x2,y2). With vertical text, baselines may be vertical. Returns false if no baseline is available.
requirements: level must be a valid PageIteratorLevel.
x1, y1, x2, y2 must be non-null pointers to receive coordinates.
Caller must handle a false return when no baseline exists at the current position.

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::RowAttributes
functions.description: Returns attributes of the current row: overall row height, descender height, and ascender height.
requirements: row_height, descenders, ascenders must be non-null pointers to receive values.
Iterator must be positioned on a row for meaningful results.

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::Orientation
functions.description: Returns orientation and layout parameters for the current block: text orientation, writing direction, textline order, and deskew angle (in radians). After making text upright, deskew_angle indicates the additional anti-clockwise rotation required to level the block, constrained to [-π/4, π/4].
requirements: orientation, writing_direction, textline_order, and deskew_angle must be non-null pointers to receive results.
Iterator must be positioned within a block.
deskew_angle will be within -Pi/4 <= angle <= Pi/4 (as documented).

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::ParagraphInfo
functions.description: Returns information about the current paragraph: justification (LEFT/RIGHT/unknown as defined), whether it appears to be a list item, whether it is a 'crown' paragraph, and the first-line indent in pixels (which may be negative). If is_crown is true, first_line_indent reports the common indent for subsequent paragraphs.
requirements: justification, is_list_item, is_crown, and first_line_indent must be non-null pointers to receive results.
Iterator must be positioned within a paragraph for meaningful results.

functions.name: tesseract::PageIterator::SetWordBlamerBundle
functions.description: If the current WERD_RES (it_->word()) is not null, sets the BlamerBundle for the current word to the provided pointer and takes ownership of it. Can only be used when iterating at the word level. Returns true on success.
requirements: Must be called while iterating at the word level (RIL_WORD).
blamer_bundle must be a valid heap-allocated pointer; ownership is transferred to the iterator/Tesseract on success (do not free after a successful call).
Returns false if the current word is null or the operation is not applicable at the current position.

functions.name: tesseract::ResultIterator::StartOfParagraph
functions.description: Factory that creates a ResultIterator positioned at the start of the paragraph that contains the position of the given LTRResultIterator. Intended to enable BiDi-aware iteration starting from the paragraph boundary.
requirements: resit must refer to a valid position within a page’s results (i.e., constructed/initialized and not at end).
The underlying recognition results referenced by resit must outlive the returned ResultIterator instance (ResultIterator relies on external data owned elsewhere).
Caller is responsible for the lifetime of the returned pointer (ownership/cleanup policy is not stated in this header; consult implementation/SDK).

functions.name: tesseract::ResultIterator::~ResultIterator
functions.description: Destructor for ResultIterator. Defaulted and virtual (overrides base), allowing safe cleanup via base-class pointers. No special action is documented.
requirements: Do not use the iterator after destruction.
Any external data the iterator references is not owned by the iterator; its lifetime must be managed elsewhere.

functions.name: tesseract::ResultIterator::Begin
functions.description: Positions the iterator at the start of the page to begin a BiDi-aware iteration in reading order.
requirements: The iterator must be properly constructed/initialized before calling Begin().
After calling Begin(), the iterator points to the first element; callers should check subsequent traversal methods (e.g., Next) for end-of-page conditions.

functions.name: tesseract::ResultIterator::Next
functions.description: Advances the iterator to the start of the next object at the specified page hierarchy level in reading order. Returns false if the end of the page is reached. Notes: RIL_SYMBOL skips non-text blocks; other levels visit each non-text block once (as a para->line->word placeholder). Iterates words in right-to-left scripts correctly if the appropriate language is loaded.
requirements: level must be a valid PageIteratorLevel.
Before the first call, call Begin() or otherwise ensure the iterator is positioned on a valid element.
The appropriate language(s) enabling RTL behavior must be loaded for correct right-to-left word iteration.
On false return, the iterator is at end-of-page; callers must not dereference/inspect current element beyond this point without repositioning.

functions.name: tesseract::ResultIterator::IsAtBeginningOf
functions.description: Returns whether the iterator is at the logical beginning of the given level (BiDi-aware), as opposed to purely left-to-right/top-to-bottom order. Otherwise behaves like PageIterator::IsAtBeginningOf().
requirements: Iterator must be positioned on a valid element at or within the queried level.
The queried level must be a valid PageIteratorLevel.

functions.name: tesseract::ResultIterator::IsAtFinalElement
functions.signature: bool tesseract::ResultIterator::IsAtFinalElement(tesseract::PageIteratorLevel level, tesseract::PageIteratorLevel element) const override;
functions.description: BiDi-correct implementation of PageIterator::IsAtFinalElement. For example, IsAtFinalElement(RIL_PARA, RIL_WORD) reports whether the current word is the last in its paragraph in logical reading order.
requirements: Iterator must be positioned on a valid element belonging to the container level specified by level.
level and element must be valid PageIteratorLevel values, where element is a child within level as per the page hierarchy.

functions.name: tesseract::ResultIterator::BlanksBeforeWord
functions.description: Returns the number of blank spaces that precede the current word.
requirements: The iterator must be positioned on a valid word (RIL_WORD) for the value to be meaningful; behavior for other levels is not documented.

functions.name: tesseract::ResultIterator::GetUTF8Text
functions.description: Returns a newly allocated, null-terminated UTF-8 string with the text for the current object at the given level. Ownership of the returned buffer is transferred to the caller.
requirements: level must be a valid PageIteratorLevel.
Iterator must be positioned on a valid element at the requested level.
Caller must release the returned buffer using delete[].
Returned text may contain line/paragraph terminators when requesting line/paragraph levels as per iterator semantics.

functions.name: tesseract::ResultIterator::GetRawLSTMTimesteps
functions.description: Returns the LSTM choices for every LSTM timestep for the current word as a pointer to a nested vector structure: [timestep][alternative][(utf8 symbol, score)]. Intended for detailed per-timestep recognition analysis.
requirements: The iterator should be positioned on a valid word; semantics for other levels are not documented.
The returned pointer may refer to internal data; ownership and lifetime are not documented here—treat as read-only and do not free unless implementation documentation states otherwise.

functions.name: tesseract::ResultIterator::GetBestLSTMSymbolChoices
functions.description: Returns the best LSTM symbol choices per position for the current word as a pointer to a vector of alternatives [(utf8 symbol, score)] per symbol position. Enables inspection of best-path symbol alternatives.
requirements: The iterator should be positioned on a valid word; semantics for other levels are not documented.
The returned pointer may refer to internal data; ownership and lifetime are not documented here—treat as read-only and do not free unless implementation documentation states otherwise.

functions.name: tesseract::ResultIterator::ParagraphIsLtr
functions.description: Reports whether the current paragraph’s dominant reading direction is left-to-right (true) as opposed to right-to-left (false).
requirements: Iterator must be positioned within a valid paragraph for a meaningful result.

functions.name: tesseract::ResultIterator::CalculateTextlineOrder
functions.signature: static void tesseract::ResultIterator::CalculateTextlineOrder(bool paragraph_is_ltr, const std::vector<tesseract::StrongScriptDirection>& word_dirs, std::vector<int>* reading_order);
functions.description: Computes the BiDi reading order for a text line given the paragraph direction and per-word strong script directions. Produces a sequence of indices (into the left-to-right word list) and optional meta-marks: kMinorRunStart, kMinorRunEnd, kComplexWord. See header examples for expected outputs in LTR/RTL paragraphs and mixed-direction runs.
requirements: reading_order must be a non-null pointer to receive the sequence.
word_dirs must contain one entry per word in the left-to-right order of the text line.
paragraph_is_ltr indicates the dominant paragraph direction and must match the paragraph containing the line.
Callers must understand and handle the negative meta-mark values (kMinorRunStart, kMinorRunEnd, kComplexWord) included in the output.

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::LTRResultIterator
functions.signature: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::LTRResultIterator(PAGE_RES *page_res, Tesseract *tesseract, int scale, int scaled_yres, int rect_left, int rect_top, int rect_width, int rect_height)
functions.description: Constructs an iterator over OCR results in strict left-to-right order, initializing iteration (Begin) immediately. It wraps internal Tesseract results (PAGE_RES) without requiring callers to access internal structures. The rectangle and scaling parameters allow mapping of tesseract image coordinates to the original image coordinates.
requirements: page_res must be obtained from TessBaseAPI internals (passed through BaseAPI) and remain valid for the lifetime of the iterator.
tesseract must be the active Tesseract instance used by the BaseAPI and remain valid for the lifetime of the iterator.

The iterator is only valid while the owning TessBaseAPI remains alive and has not been modified by calls such as Init, SetImage, Recognize, Clear, End, DetectOS, or other calls that change the internal PAGE_RES.
rect_left and rect_top are top-left-origin coordinates of the rectangle in the original image; output boxes from the iterator must be offset by these to get original-image coordinates.
If the Thresholder scaled the image, tesseract coordinates must be divided by scale before adding (rect_left, rect_top).
scaled_yres is the effective resolution (dpi) of the binary image seen by Tesseract; pass the value provided by the Thresholder/BaseAPI.
After construction, iteration is positioned at the beginning (Begin already called).

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::~LTRResultIterator
functions.description: Destroys the LTRResultIterator and releases any iterator-related resources. Does not free data owned by the TessBaseAPI.
requirements: Do not use the iterator after destruction.
Ensure no ongoing access to pointers returned by this iterator after it is destroyed (for example, font attribute name pointers).

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::GetUTF8Text
functions.description: Returns a newly allocated, null-terminated UTF-8 string containing the recognized text for the current object at the given page hierarchy level.
requirements: The iterator must be positioned on a valid object at the requested level.
Caller must free the returned buffer with delete[].
level must be a valid PageIteratorLevel value.

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::SetLineSeparator
functions.description: Sets the string inserted at the end of each text line when generating text via this iterator (default is "\n").
requirements: new_line must point to a valid null-terminated string.
The provided pointer may be stored internally; ensure it remains valid for the lifetime of the iterator or until replaced.

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::SetParagraphSeparator
functions.description: Sets the string inserted at the end of each paragraph when generating text via this iterator (default is "\n").
requirements: new_para must point to a valid null-terminated string.
The provided pointer may be stored internally; ensure it remains valid for the lifetime of the iterator or until replaced.

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::Confidence
functions.description: Returns the mean confidence for the current object at the specified level. Interpreted as a percent probability in the range 0.0f–100.0f.
requirements: The iterator must be positioned on a valid object at the requested level.
level must be a valid PageIteratorLevel value.
Caller should interpret the return as a percentage (0.0f–100.0f).

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::WordFontAttributes
functions.signature: const char * tesseract::LTRResultIterator::WordFontAttributes(bool *is_bold, bool *is_italic, bool *is_underlined, bool *is_monospace, bool *is_serif, bool *is_smallcaps, int *pointsize, int *font_id) const
functions.description: Returns the font name and font attributes for the current word. If iterating at a higher level than words (e.g., textlines), attributes of the first word in that unit are returned. Point size is in printer’s points (1/72 inch).
requirements: The iterator must be positioned on a word, or a higher level where a first word exists.
Returned const char* points to internal storage; do NOT delete it. Its lifetime matches the iterator and is invalidated by TessBaseAPI calls like Init, SetImage, End, or by destroying the iterator.
Output pointer parameters (if non-null) will be filled with the corresponding attributes.
font_id and other pointers must be valid writable pointers if provided.

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::WordRecognitionLanguage
functions.description: Returns the name of the language used to recognize the current word, or nullptr on error.
requirements: The iterator must be positioned on a valid word or higher-level element containing a word.
Do not delete the returned pointer; it refers to internal storage.
Caller must handle a nullptr return on error.

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::WordDirection
functions.description: Returns the overall script directionality of the current word (e.g., left-to-right or right-to-left). If at a higher level, uses the first word of that unit.
requirements: The iterator must be positioned on a valid word or higher-level element containing a word.

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::WordIsFromDictionary
functions.description: Indicates whether the current word was found in a dictionary.
requirements: The iterator must be positioned on a valid word or higher-level element containing a word.

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::BlanksBeforeWord
functions.description: Returns the number of blank characters preceding the current word.
requirements: The iterator must be positioned on a valid word or higher-level element containing a word.

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::WordIsNumeric
functions.description: Returns true if the current word is numeric.
requirements: The iterator must be positioned on a valid word or higher-level element containing a word.

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::HasBlamerInfo
functions.description: Returns true if the current word contains blamer information.
requirements: The iterator must be positioned on a valid word or higher-level element containing a word.

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::GetParamsTrainingBundle
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the ParamsTrainingBundle stored in the current word’s BlamerBundle.
requirements: Call only if HasBlamerInfo() returns true; otherwise the return may be nullptr or invalid.
The returned pointer is to internal data; do not free or modify.

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::GetBlamerDebug
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a string containing blamer debug information for the current word.
requirements: Assumes the word’s blamer_bundle is not nullptr; call HasBlamerInfo() first to ensure availability.
The returned pointer refers to internal storage; do not delete.

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::GetBlamerMisadaptionDebug
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a string containing misadaption information from the blamer for the current word.
requirements: Assumes the word’s blamer_bundle is not nullptr; call HasBlamerInfo() first to ensure availability.
The returned pointer refers to internal storage; do not delete.

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::HasTruthString
functions.description: Returns true if a truth string (ground truth) was recorded for the current word.
requirements: The iterator must be positioned on a valid word or higher-level element containing a word.

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::EquivalentToTruth
functions.description: Returns true if the provided UTF-8 string is equivalent to the recorded truth string for the current word.
requirements: The iterator must be positioned on a valid word or higher-level element containing a word.
str must be a valid null-terminated UTF-8 string.
Meaningful comparison requires that HasTruthString() is true.

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::WordTruthUTF8Text
functions.description: Returns a newly allocated null-terminated UTF-8 truth string for the current word.
requirements: The iterator must be positioned on a valid word or higher-level element containing a word.
Caller must free the returned buffer with delete[].
If no truth string exists, behavior is library-defined (may return nullptr or empty string); caller should check HasTruthString().

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::WordNormedUTF8Text
functions.description: Returns a newly allocated null-terminated UTF-8 normalized OCR string for the current word.
requirements: The iterator must be positioned on a valid word or higher-level element containing a word.
Caller must free the returned buffer with delete[].

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::WordLattice
functions.description: Returns a pointer to serialized choice lattice data for the current word and writes the total byte size to lattice_size.
requirements: The iterator must be positioned on a valid word or higher-level element containing a word.
lattice_size must be a valid non-null pointer to int to receive the size.
The returned pointer refers to internally owned data; do not delete or modify.
Caller must not use the returned pointer after the iterator or its owning TessBaseAPI is invalidated.

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::SymbolIsSuperscript
functions.description: Returns true if the current symbol is a superscript. If at a higher level (e.g., words), returns the attribute of the first symbol in that unit.
requirements: The iterator must be positioned on a valid symbol or higher-level element containing a symbol.

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::SymbolIsSubscript
functions.description: Returns true if the current symbol is a subscript. If at a higher level (e.g., words), returns the attribute of the first symbol in that unit.
requirements: The iterator must be positioned on a valid symbol or higher-level element containing a symbol.

functions.name: tesseract::LTRResultIterator::SymbolIsDropcap
functions.description: Returns true if the current symbol is a drop cap. If at a higher level (e.g., words), returns the attribute of the first symbol in that unit.
requirements: The iterator must be positioned on a valid symbol or higher-level element containing a symbol.

functions.name: tesseract::ChoiceIterator::ChoiceIterator
functions.description: Constructs an iterator over the classifier choices for the symbol referenced by the given LTRResultIterator. Supports a one-shot iteration over the symbol’s choices.

The underlying LTRResultIterator and its owning TessBaseAPI must remain valid while iterating choices.

functions.name: tesseract::ChoiceIterator::~ChoiceIterator
functions.description: Destroys the ChoiceIterator and releases any internal resources associated with the choice iteration.
requirements: Do not use the iterator after destruction.
Pointers returned by this iterator (e.g., from GetUTF8Text or Timesteps) must not be used after destruction.

functions.name: tesseract::ChoiceIterator::Next
functions.description: Advances to the next classifier choice for the current symbol. Returns false when there are no more choices.

Call until it returns false to exhaust all choices. Do not continue calling after it returns false.

functions.name: tesseract::ChoiceIterator::GetUTF8Text
functions.description: Returns a null-terminated UTF-8 string for the currently selected choice. The pointer refers to internal storage and must not be freed by the caller.
requirements: ChoiceIterator must be positioned on a valid choice (e.g., immediately after construction or after a successful Next()).
Do not delete or modify the returned pointer.
Do not use the returned pointer after the iterator is destroyed or advanced if the storage is per-choice.

functions.description: Returns the confidence of the current choice. For LSTM-only traineddata the value is 0.0f–1.0f and the choices for a symbol roughly sum to 1.0f; for legacy-engine-only traineddata the value is a percent (0.0f–100.0f) and choices do not sum to 100.
requirements: ChoiceIterator must be positioned on a valid choice.
Interpret the range according to the engine/traineddata in use as described.

functions.name: tesseract::ChoiceIterator::Timesteps
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a vector of timesteps for the current symbol. Each timestep is a vector of (symbol, probability) pairs representing the LSTM per-timestep distribution.
requirements: Only meaningful when LSTM-related traineddata is used; otherwise content may be empty or unspecified.
The returned pointer refers to data owned/managed by the iterator; do not free it.
Do not use the returned pointer after the iterator is destroyed.

functions.name: tesseract::TessResultRenderer::~TessResultRenderer
functions.description: Virtual destructor for TessResultRenderer. Cleans up any resources owned by the renderer chain. Intended to be called implicitly when a renderer object is destroyed.

If the renderer owns chained renderers (insert took ownership), their lifetimes are managed by this object; callers must not delete those separately.

next may be a chain headed by a TessResultRenderer whose own next() is non-null; insert will append the sequences (as documented).

functions.name: tesseract::TessResultRenderer::next
functions.description: Returns the next renderer in the chain, or nullptr if none. Used to iterate a chain of renderers composed via insert.

functions.name: tesseract::TessResultRenderer::BeginDocument
functions.description: Starts a new output document and clears any existing accumulated output data. Title should be UTF-8. Must be called before AddImage and EndDocument for a given document lifecycle.
requirements: title should use UTF-8 encoding (as documented).
BeginDocument must be called before AddImage and EndDocument for a document.
Calling BeginDocument starts a new document and clears prior output data.

functions.description: Adds the recognized text (and format-specific data) from the source image in the provided TessBaseAPI to the current document. Invalid if BeginDocument has not been called. Designed to fit with TessBaseAPI’s internal state.
requirements: BeginDocument must have been successfully called for the current document before calling AddImage (otherwise invalid).
api must be a valid, non-null pointer to a TessBaseAPI instance (inferred from usage).
api is expected to be in a state suitable for extracting recognition results for the current image (inferred from name and comments).

functions.name: tesseract::TessResultRenderer::EndDocument
functions.description: Finalizes and closes the current document’s output. Invalid if BeginDocument has not been called. After successful completion, the document’s output is complete.
requirements: BeginDocument must have been successfully called for the current document before calling EndDocument (otherwise invalid).

functions.name: tesseract::TessResultRenderer::file_extension
functions.description: Returns the standard file extension associated with this renderer’s output (for example, "pdf", "hocr").

functions.name: tesseract::TessResultRenderer::title
functions.description: Returns the UTF-8 title string for the current (or most recent) document.

functions.name: tesseract::TessResultRenderer::happy
functions.description: Reports whether the renderer is in a good state (e.g., no disk/full errors encountered).

functions.name: tesseract::TessResultRenderer::imagenum
functions.description: Returns the index of the last image passed to AddImage. Returns -1 if a document was never started. Increments regardless of render success.
