This constructor is only available if the build is not compiled with DISABLED_LEGACY_ENGINE (as guarded by the header).

functions.name: tesseract::OSResults::update_best_orientation
functions.description: Recomputes and stores the best (most likely) page orientation based on the accumulated orientation scores in this OSResults instance. Intended to be called after updating orientation scores to refresh best_result. Exact scoring details are not provided in this header.
requirements: The OSResults instance must have valid orientation scores in orientations[4].
Callers should ensure any concurrent updates to orientations are completed before calling this function.
Details of how best_result is updated are unknown; ensure OSResults is properly initialized.

functions.name: tesseract::OSResults::set_best_orientation
functions.description: Explicitly sets the best estimated orientation to the provided orientation_id without recomputing scores. Useful to override or seed the orientation decision.
requirements: orientation_id must be in the range [0,3], mapping to clockwise rotations [0, 270, 180, 90] degrees respectively, as documented in the header.
Call this only when you intend to override the computed best orientation.

functions.name: tesseract::OSResults::update_best_script
functions.description: Updates or computes the best estimated script for the specified orientation based on scripts_na[orientation_id][]. Stores the decision in best_result.
requirements: orientation_id must be in the range [0,3].
scripts_na[orientation_id][] must contain valid accumulated script confidence scores.
Call after populating scripts_na for the given orientation.

functions.name: tesseract::OSResults::get_best_script
functions.description: Returns the index of the highest-scoring script for the specified orientation using the scripts_na matrix. Intended for querying the most likely script under a fixed orientation.
requirements: orientation_id must be in the range [0,3].
scripts_na[orientation_id][] must have been populated with scores before calling.

functions.name: tesseract::OSResults::accumulate
functions.description: Accumulates orientation and script scores from another OSResults into this one and updates the best script accordingly. Useful for combining results across blobs/blocks/pages.
requirements: The source OSResults reference must be a valid, initialized object.
Both OSResults should be considered compatible (e.g., same script index space). This is inferred from usage; exact compatibility requirements are unknown.
Callers should avoid integer overflow or unintended scaling; accumulation method details are not specified.

functions.name: tesseract::OSResults::print_scores
functions.description: Prints statistics/scores for all orientations and scripts contained in this OSResults. Intended for debugging or diagnostics.
requirements: The OSResults instance must be initialized.
Output destination/details are not specified; assumed to print to a standard logging/IO stream.

functions.name: tesseract::OSResults::print_scores
functions.description: Prints statistics/scores for the specified orientation. Intended for targeted diagnostics of one orientation index.
requirements: orientation_id must be in the range [0,3].
The OSResults instance must be initialized.

functions.name: tesseract::OrientationDetector::OrientationDetector
functions.description: Constructs an OrientationDetector configured with an optional allowed script set and a target OSResults to accumulate orientation detection results. Used to evaluate blob-level orientation evidence.
requirements: results must point to a valid tesseract::OSResults object whose lifetime exceeds that of the detector.
If provided, allowed_scripts must point to a valid std::vector<int> describing allowed script IDs; passing nullptr implies no restriction (inferred; exact behavior not documented).

functions.name: tesseract::OrientationDetector::detect_blob
functions.description: Analyzes a blob’s recognition scores to update orientation-related evidence in OSResults and returns whether the blob contributed usable orientation information. Exact heuristics are not specified here.
requirements: scores must be a valid, non-null pointer to a BLOB_CHOICE_LIST containing recognition alternatives for a single blob.
The associated OSResults provided at construction must remain valid.
Return semantics beyond boolean success are unknown.

functions.name: tesseract::OrientationDetector::get_orientation
functions.description: Returns the currently estimated best orientation as an orientation id (0..3) based on accumulated evidence.
requirements: The detector must have been constructed with a valid OSResults pointer.
Orientation id mapping to degrees follows [0, 270, 180, 90] clockwise rotations as documented in the header.

functions.name: tesseract::ScriptDetector::ScriptDetector
functions.description: Constructs a ScriptDetector with an optional set of allowed scripts, an OSResults for accumulation, and a Tesseract engine for accessing script information. Used to gather script evidence at the blob level.
requirements: osr must point to a valid tesseract::OSResults instance for the lifetime of the detector.
tess must point to a valid tesseract::Tesseract engine configured with the relevant unicharset/script data.
If provided, allowed_scripts must point to a valid std::vector<int> of allowed script IDs; passing nullptr implies no restriction (inferred; exact behavior not documented).

functions.name: tesseract::ScriptDetector::detect_blob
functions.description: Processes a blob’s recognition scores to update script confidence statistics in OSResults for one or more orientations. Exact scoring and script-ID mapping are not detailed here.
requirements: scores must be a valid, non-null pointer to a BLOB_CHOICE_LIST representing choices for a single blob.
The OSResults and Tesseract pointers supplied at construction must remain valid.
Caller should ensure scores correspond to the same script index space as OSResults (inferred).

functions.name: tesseract::ScriptDetector::must_stop
functions.description: Returns whether detection can stop early for the specified orientation, presumably after reaching a confident script decision or threshold. Specific criteria are not documented in this header.
requirements: orientation must be in the range [0,3].
The detector must have been initialized properly; relies on internal state built during detection.

functions.name: tesseract::orientation_and_script_detection
functions.description: High-level entry point that performs orientation and script detection on the document specified by filename, populating the provided OSResults using the given Tesseract engine. Returns an integer status code; exact semantics are not specified here.
requirements: filename must be a valid, non-null C-string path to an input image/document readable by Tesseract.
The OSResults pointer must be valid and initialized; it will be populated with detection results.
The Tesseract pointer must refer to a properly initialized engine configured with the appropriate language/script data.
Return code meaning is unknown; callers should treat non-zero/zero as library-defined.

functions.name: tesseract::os_detect
functions.description: Runs orientation/script detection over the provided list of text blocks, accumulating results into osr using tess for script/orientation data. Returns an integer status; details not provided here.
requirements: port_blocks must be a valid, non-null pointer to a TO_BLOCK_LIST containing blocks to analyze.
osr must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized OSResults to receive accumulated scores.
tess must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized Tesseract engine.

functions.name: tesseract::os_detect_blobs
functions.signature: int tesseract::os_detect_blobs(const std::vector<int> *allowed_scripts, tesseract::BLOBNBOX_CLIST *blob_list, tesseract::OSResults *osr, tesseract::Tesseract *tess)
functions.description: Performs orientation and script detection over a list of blobs, optionally restricting to allowed scripts, updating osr via tess. Returns an integer status code; exact meaning is unspecified.
requirements: If provided, allowed_scripts must point to a valid std::vector<int> of allowed script IDs; passing nullptr implies no restriction (inferred; behavior not documented).
blob_list must be a valid, non-null pointer to a BLOBNBOX_CLIST of blobs to analyze.
osr must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized OSResults object.
tess must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized Tesseract engine.

functions.name: tesseract::os_detect_blob
functions.description: Runs detection on a single blob using the provided OrientationDetector and ScriptDetector, updating OSResults as appropriate, and returns whether the blob produced usable detection information. Exact update rules are not specified here.
requirements: bbox must be a valid, non-null pointer to a BLOBNBOX representing the blob to analyze.
o must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized OrientationDetector associated with the same OSResults.
s must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized ScriptDetector associated with the same OSResults and tess.
The OSResults and Tesseract pointers must be valid and consistent with the detectors.

functions.name: tesseract::OrientationIdToValue
functions.description: Converts an orientation index to its corresponding clockwise rotation in degrees required to make text upright. The mapping is: id 0 -> 0°, 1 -> 270°, 2 -> 180°, 3 -> 90°. Returns the degree value.
requirements: id must be in the range [0,3]; other values are undefined.
The function is pure conversion with no side effects.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::TessBaseAPI
functions.description: Default constructor for the Tesseract OCR API wrapper. Initializes an instance without loading language data. Only a subset of methods (up to and including SetVariable notes) may be called before Init().
requirements: Must call Init(...) successfully before invoking recognition-related methods (e.g., SetImage/Recognize/Get*Text).
Multiple instances can be used in parallel threads, but setting certain global params (classify/textord) via SetVariable affects all instances.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::~TessBaseAPI
functions.description: Destructor. Releases all resources held by the API instance. Equivalent to calling End() then destroying the object.
requirements: After destruction, the instance must not be used.
If using iterators pointing to internal data, they must be deleted before the API instance is destroyed.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::Version
functions.description: Returns a static C-string with the Tesseract version identifier. The returned pointer must not be freed by the caller.
requirements: Return value is a static string; do not delete or modify it.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::SetInputName
functions.description: Sets the logical input filename for the current document/image. Used for training, UNLV zone file reading, and embedding original image in searchable PDF outputs.
requirements: name may be nullptr if unknown, but some features (e.g., PDF embedding) may rely on it.
Call before processing pages if you need file-based side effects.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetInputName
functions.description: Returns the previously set input filename string pointer.
requirements: Returned pointer remains owned by TessBaseAPI; do not free.
Value is meaningful only if previously set via SetInputName or implicitly by input pipelines.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::SetInputImage
functions.description: Sets the original input image Pix for use in outputs (e.g., searchable PDF) when direct file embedding is not possible. Ownership of pix is transferred to the API.
requirements: pix must be a valid Leptonica Pix*.
Caller must not use or destroy pix after passing; TessBaseAPI takes ownership.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetInputImage
functions.description: Returns the stored original input image Pix pointer if set via SetInputImage. Ownership is not transferred.
requirements: Returned Pix* is owned by TessBaseAPI; do not pixDestroy it.
May return nullptr if no input image was set.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetSourceYResolution
functions.description: Returns the Y-axis resolution (DPI) of the source image, used for PDF metadata and font-size estimation.
requirements: Meaningful value requires that an image has been provided (SetImage/TesseractRect) or the source metadata is available; otherwise may be unspecified.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetDatapath
functions.description: Returns the datapath (tessdata directory path) used by the last successful Init.
requirements: Returned pointer remains owned by TessBaseAPI; do not free.
Valid after successful Init.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::SetOutputName
functions.description: Sets the base name for auxiliary debug output files.
requirements: Intended for debugging; call before operations that emit such files.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::SetVariable
functions.description: Sets a non-init Tesseract parameter by name to the given value (as string), similar to config file entries. Returns false if parameter was not found. Settings persist until End().
requirements: Must be called after Init() for effect on non-init parameters; settings made before Init() revert on End().
name must match an existing parameter; otherwise returns false.
value must be a valid textual representation for the parameter type.
Using certain global params (in classify/textord) affects all instances across threads.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::SetDebugVariable
functions.description: Sets a debug-only Tesseract parameter by name to value. Returns false if the parameter is not found.
requirements: Primarily for parameters containing 'debug' in the name.
name must exist; otherwise returns false.
Effect after Init().

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetIntVariable
functions.description: Looks up an integer parameter by name and writes its current value to value. Returns true if found.
requirements: value must be a valid non-null pointer.
name must refer to an integer parameter.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetBoolVariable
functions.description: Looks up a boolean parameter by name and writes its current value to value. Returns true if found.
requirements: value must be a valid non-null pointer.
name must refer to a boolean parameter.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetDoubleVariable
functions.description: Looks up a double-precision parameter by name and writes its current value to value. Returns true if found.
requirements: value must be a valid non-null pointer.
name must refer to a double parameter.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetStringVariable
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the string value of the named parameter if found; otherwise returns nullptr. The returned pointer is owned by Tesseract.
requirements: name must refer to an existing string parameter.
Returned pointer must not be freed by caller.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::PrintFontsTable
functions.description: Prints Tesseract's fonts table to the provided FILE stream. Available only when legacy engine is enabled (not compiled with DISABLED_LEGACY_ENGINE).
requirements: fp must be a valid writable FILE*.
Availability depends on build-time macro: DISABLED_LEGACY_ENGINE must not be defined.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::PrintVariables
functions.description: Prints all Tesseract parameters and their values to the given FILE stream.
requirements: fp must be a valid writable FILE*.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetVariableAsString
functions.description: Gets the value of the named parameter as a std::string if it exists, storing it in val. Returns true if found.
requirements: val must be a valid non-null pointer.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::Init
functions.signature: int tesseract::TessBaseAPI::Init(const char *datapath, const char *language, OcrEngineMode mode, char **configs, int configs_size, const std::vector<std::string> *vars_vec, const std::vector<std::string> *vars_values, bool set_only_non_debug_params)
functions.description: Initializes the OCR engine with the specified tessdata path, languages, engine mode, optional config files, and parameter overrides. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure. Resets parameters to language defaults on language change.
requirements: datapath must point to a tessdata directory; may be nullptr if default search paths are used by the library (implementation-defined).
language may be nullptr (defaults to "eng") or a composite like "hin+eng"; prefixes '~' suppress auto-loaded dependencies.
configs must point to an array of configs_size C-strings or be nullptr with size 0.
If vars_vec/vars_values are provided, they must be same length; entries correspond to parameter names and values; if set_only_non_debug_params is true, only non-debug params are set.
On re-Init with a different language, all parameters reset to defaults.
Thread-safety: multiple instances OK; setting some global params may affect all instances.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetInitLanguagesAsString
functions.description: Returns the languages string explicitly requested in the last successful Init (e.g., "deu+hin"). Auto-loaded dependencies are not included. Returned pointer is owned by Tesseract.
requirements: Valid only after a successful Init.
Do not free the returned pointer.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetLoadedLanguagesAsVector
functions.description: Fills langs with all languages actually loaded in the last Init, including dependencies.
requirements: langs must be a valid non-null pointer.
Valid after successful Init.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetAvailableLanguagesAsVector
functions.description: Populates langs with the available languages discovered in the datapath, sorted.
requirements: langs must be a valid non-null pointer.
Requires a valid datapath (typically after Init) or otherwise depends on internal search paths.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::InitForAnalysePage
functions.description: Initializes the API for page layout analysis only. Recognition calls will error out. Intended for SetImage + AnalyseLayout workflows.
requirements: Call before AnalyseLayout when recognition is not needed.
Do not call recognition methods (e.g., GetUTF8Text) after this unless a full Init is performed.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::ReadConfigFile
functions.description: Reads a configuration file of param=value pairs from standard locations or a supplied path. Only non-init parameters are set; init parameters must be provided via Init().
requirements: filename must reference a readable config file in tessdata/configs, tessdata/tessconfigs, or an explicit path.
A successful Init should precede to persist non-init changes across use.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::ReadDebugConfigFile
functions.description: Reads a configuration file and sets only debug parameters contained therein.
requirements: filename must reference a readable config file.
Only parameters considered debug will be set.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::SetPageSegMode
functions.description: Sets the page segmentation mode (PSM). Stored internally as an IntParam, so it can also be set via configs or SetVariable("tessedit_pageseg_mode", ...).
requirements: mode must be a valid PageSegMode enum value.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetPageSegMode
functions.description: Gets the current page segmentation mode (PSM).

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::TesseractRect
functions.signature: char * tesseract::TessBaseAPI::TesseractRect(const unsigned char *imagedata, int bytes_per_pixel, int bytes_per_line, int left, int top, int width, int height)
functions.description: Convenience API: Recognizes text in the given sub-rectangle of an image buffer and returns UTF-8 text. Handles 8bpp grayscale, 24/32bpp color, or 1bpp packed binary (set bytes_per_pixel=0). Caller must delete[] the returned string.
requirements: imagedata must point to at least (top+height-1) rows and required columns using bytes_per_line stride.
For 1bpp, data must be MSB-first bit-packed with 1=WHITE and bytes_per_pixel must be 0.
left, top, width, height must define a rectangle within the image bounds.
Must have successfully called Init() prior to use.
Caller must free result with delete[].

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::ClearAdaptiveClassifier
functions.description: Clears adaptive classifier data between pages/documents to reduce carry-over effects.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::SetImage
functions.signature: void tesseract::TessBaseAPI::SetImage(const unsigned char *imagedata, int width, int height, int bytes_per_pixel, int bytes_per_line)
functions.description: Provides an image buffer for recognition. The buffer is copied and converted to Leptonica Pix internally. Clears previous results and sets the recognition rectangle to the full image.
requirements: imagedata must be valid for the specified width/height and bytes_per_line stride.
bytes_per_pixel must correspond to supported formats (1bpp via TesseractRect special-case, otherwise typical 1/3/4).
Must call Init() before providing images for recognition.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::SetSourceResolution
functions.description: Sets the source image resolution (pixels per inch) to improve font size estimation and metadata. Call after SetImage().
requirements: ppi should be a positive integer reflecting true image DPI.
Call after SetImage().

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::SetRectangle
functions.signature: void tesseract::TessBaseAPI::SetRectangle(int left, int top, int width, int height)
functions.description: Restricts recognition to a sub-rectangle of the current image. Clears prior recognition results so multiple rectangles can be processed on the same image.
requirements: Must have set an image via SetImage first.
Rectangle must lie within the image bounds.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetThresholdedImage
functions.description: Returns a copy of the internal thresholded (binarized) image as a Leptonica Pix. Caller owns the returned Pix and must destroy it with pixDestroy().
requirements: Must be called after SetImage (or TesseractRect).
Caller must pixDestroy() the returned Pix.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetGradient
functions.description: Returns the average gradient (skew/tilt indicator) of text lines on the page.
requirements: Requires that an image has been set and layout analysis has occurred implicitly or explicitly.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetRegions
functions.description: Performs/uses page layout analysis to return image regions in reading order as a Boxa/Pixa pair. Can be called before or after Recognize.
requirements: pixa may be non-null to receive region images; caller must call boxaDestroy() and pixaDestroy() on outputs.
Requires an image to have been set.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetTextlines
functions.signature: Boxa * tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetTextlines(bool raw_image, int raw_padding, Pixa **pixa, int **blockids, int **paraids)
functions.description: Returns textlines (and optionally their images) as Boxa/Pixa in reading order. Can use raw input image with padding or the thresholded image. Optionally returns block and paragraph ids per line.
requirements: If pixa is non-null, caller must destroy returned Pixa with pixaDestroy().
Caller must destroy returned Boxa with boxaDestroy().
If blockids/paraids are non-null, caller must delete[] the arrays.
Requires an image to have been set.
If raw_image is true, raw_padding must be >= 0.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetStrips
functions.description: Returns textlines and strips (non-rectangular region handling) as Boxa/Pixa in reading order, with optional block ids.
requirements: Caller must destroy returned Boxa and Pixa (if provided).
If blockids is non-null, caller must delete[] it.
Requires an image to have been set.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetWords
functions.description: Returns word bounding boxes and optional word images as Boxa/Pixa in reading order.
requirements: Caller must destroy returned Boxa and Pixa (if provided).
Requires an image to have been set.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetConnectedComponents
functions.description: Returns connected text components (post-segmentation, pre-recognition) as Boxa/Pixa in reading order.
requirements: Caller must call boxaDestroy() on returned Boxa and pixaDestroy() on returned Pixa (if provided).
Can be called before or after Recognize.
Requires an image to have been set.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetComponentImages
functions.signature: Boxa * tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetComponentImages(PageIteratorLevel level, bool text_only, bool raw_image, int raw_padding, Pixa **pixa, int **blockids, int **paraids)
functions.description: Returns components at the requested level (block, textline, word, etc.) as Boxa/Pixa in reading order. Can optionally extract from raw image with padding and restrict to text-only components. Optionally returns block and paragraph ids.
requirements: Caller must destroy returned Boxa and Pixa (if provided).
If blockids or paraids are provided, caller must delete[] the arrays.
Requires an image to have been set.
If raw_image is true, raw_padding must be >= 0.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetThresholdedImageScaleFactor
functions.description: Returns the scale factor of the internally generated thresholded image as used by GetThresholdedImage and related APIs. Returns 0 if no thresholder is set.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::AnalyseLayout
functions.description: Runs page layout analysis in the current PSM and returns a PageIterator over the layout results. Iterator must be deleted by the caller. Points to internal data; invalidated by Init, SetImage, Recognize, Clear, End, DetectOS, etc.
requirements: An image must have been set.
Caller must delete the returned PageIterator.
Do not use the iterator after state-changing API calls listed in the warning.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::Recognize
functions.description: Performs recognition on the current image (and rectangle), generating internal results. Returns 0 on success. Optional monitor can receive progress and support cancellation.
requirements: Must call SetImage (and optionally SetRectangle) beforehand.
monitor may be nullptr for no callbacks.
After Recognize, results persist until next SetImage.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::ProcessPages
functions.signature: bool tesseract::TessBaseAPI::ProcessPages(const char *filename, const char *retry_config, int timeout_millisec, tesseract::TessResultRenderer *renderer)
functions.description: High-level API to process one or more images: filename can be a single image, a multi-page TIFF, or a text file listing images. Produces output via the provided renderer. Optional retry_config can be used for fallback on failure. Returns true on success.
requirements: Must have successfully called Init().
renderer must be a valid renderer configured for desired output (e.g., text, PDF).
timeout_millisec=0 means no timeout; positive values enforce per-page timeout.
If tessedit_page_number is set (via params), only that page is processed.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::ProcessPagesInternal
functions.signature: bool tesseract::TessBaseAPI::ProcessPagesInternal(const char *filename, const char *retry_config, int timeout_millisec, tesseract::TessResultRenderer *renderer)
functions.description: Internal worker for ProcessPages. Same behavior/parameters; exposed for advanced control.
requirements: Same as ProcessPages.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::ProcessPage
functions.signature: bool tesseract::TessBaseAPI::ProcessPage(Pix *pix, int page_index, const char *filename, const char *retry_config, int timeout_millisec, tesseract::TessResultRenderer *renderer)
functions.description: Processes a single image Pix and emits output via renderer. filename and page_index are used for side effects like reading box files or hOCR metadata. Returns true on success.
requirements: Must have successfully called Init().
pix must be a valid Leptonica Pix*.
renderer must be non-null and appropriately configured.
timeout_millisec=0 means no timeout.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetIterator
functions.description: Returns a read-only iterator over recognition/layout results. Caller must delete it. Iterator references internal data and is invalidated by many state changes (Init, SetImage, Recognize, Clear, End, DetectOS, etc.).
requirements: Must have performed recognition or layout analysis first (implicitly or via Recognize/AnalyseLayout).
Caller must delete the returned iterator.
Do not use the iterator after state changes listed.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetMutableIterator
functions.description: Returns a mutable iterator over recognition/layout results. Same lifetime and invalidation rules as GetIterator. Caller must delete it.
requirements: Same as GetIterator.
Caller must delete the returned iterator.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetUTF8Text
functions.description: Returns the recognized text as a UTF-8 encoded C-string. Triggers recognition if needed. Caller must free with delete[].
requirements: Must have called Init() and SetImage (and optional SetRectangle).
Caller must delete[] the returned string.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetHOCRText
functions.description: Returns an hOCR HTML-formatted UTF-8 string for the given 0-based page_number, with optional progress/cancellation via monitor. Caller must delete[].
requirements: page_number is 0-based in API but appears 1-based in output.
Caller must delete[] the returned string.
monitor may be nullptr.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetAltoText
functions.description: Returns an XML string with ALTO markup for the given 0-based page_number. Caller must delete[].
requirements: Caller must delete[] the returned string.
monitor may be nullptr.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetPAGEText
functions.description: Returns an XML string with PAGE markup for the given 0-based page_number. Caller must delete[].
requirements: Caller must delete[] the returned string.
monitor may be nullptr.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetTSVText
functions.description: Returns a UTF-8 TSV-formatted string of recognition results for the specified 0-based page_number. Caller must delete[].
requirements: Caller must delete[] the returned string.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetLSTMBoxText
functions.description: Returns a UTF-8 string containing box data formatted for LSTM training, using coordinates in the original image. Caller must delete[].
requirements: Caller must delete[] the returned string.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetBoxText
functions.description: Returns a UTF-8 string in classic box file format using original image coordinates for the specified 0-based page_number. Caller must delete[].
requirements: Caller must delete[] the returned string.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetWordStrBoxText
functions.description: Returns a UTF-8 string in WordStr box file format for the specified 0-based page_number. Caller must delete[].
requirements: Caller must delete[] the returned string.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetUNLVText
functions.description: Returns recognized text encoded as UNLV format Latin-1 with specific reject/suspect codes. Caller must delete[].
requirements: Caller must delete[] the returned string.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::DetectOrientationScript
functions.description: Detects the image orientation (0/90/180/270 degrees clockwise) and apparent script name, returning confidence values. Returns true on success and writes results to outputs.
requirements: All output pointers provided must be valid non-null pointers to receive values.
An image must have been set.
script_name points to an internal static/owned string; do not free.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetOsdText
functions.description: Returns a UTF-8 string with orientation and script detection (OSD) info for the given 0-based page_number. Caller must delete[].
requirements: Caller must delete[] the returned string.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::MeanTextConf
functions.description: Returns the average confidence value (0–100) over recognized text.
requirements: Meaningful only after recognition results are available.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::AllWordConfidences
functions.description: Returns an array of per-word confidence values (0–100), terminated by -1. Caller must delete[] the returned array.
requirements: Caller must delete[] the returned int array.
The number of confidences corresponds to space-delimited words in GetUTF8Text().

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::AdaptToWordStr
functions.description: [Legacy-engine only] Adapts the classifier to a single word, given as space-delimited UTF-8 graphemes (e.g., "l i k e"). Assumes the image/rectangle corresponds to that word. Preserves current PSM; uses provided mode (e.g., PSM_SINGLE_WORD or PSM_CIRCLE_WORD) for layout. Returns false if adaptation is not possible.
requirements: Requires legacy engine availability (not compiled with DISABLED_LEGACY_ENGINE).
Must have an image set and rectangle corresponding to the word.
wordstr must be space-delimited UTF-8 graphemes.
mode should be PSM_SINGLE_WORD or PSM_CIRCLE_WORD.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::Clear
functions.description: Clears stored image data and recognition results without freeing heavy persistent recognition data. After calling, you must SetImage or TesseractRect before recognizing again.
requirements: Do not call recognition APIs until a new image is set.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::End
functions.description: Shuts down the engine and frees all memory. After End(), only Init and methods declared before Init in the class may be called.
requirements: After End(), do not call other API functions except those permitted (e.g., Init and earlier).

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::ClearPersistentCache
functions.description: Clears library-level global caches (e.g., dictionaries) that persist across API instances and Init/End cycles.
requirements: Affects all instances within the process.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::IsValidWord
functions.description: Checks whether word is valid according to the current language model. Returns 0 if invalid, non-zero if valid. Marked as temporary API.
requirements: word must be a UTF-8 C-string.
Depends on initialized language model; call after Init().

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::IsValidCharacter
functions.description: Returns true if the UTF-8 character is defined in the current UNICHARSET.
requirements: utf8_character must point to a single valid UTF-8 character sequence.
Call after Init() for a meaningful UNICHARSET.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetTextDirection
functions.description: Estimates text direction on the page, returning offset and slope. Returns true on success.
requirements: out_offset and out_slope must be non-null pointers.
Requires image/layout analysis to have been performed implicitly or explicitly.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::SetDictFunc
functions.description: Overrides the dictionary's letter_is_okay_ function with the provided member-function pointer.
requirements: f must be a valid pointer to a compatible Dict member function.
Affects behavior of the internal dictionary during recognition.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::SetProbabilityInContextFunc
functions.description: Overrides Dict::probability_in_context_ with the provided member-function pointer to customize contextual probabilities.
requirements: f must be a valid pointer to a compatible Dict member function.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::DetectOS
functions.description: Estimates orientation and script of the image, writing results into the provided OSResults. Returns true on successful processing.
requirements: Pointer argument must be valid and non-null to receive results.
Requires an image to have been set.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetBlockTextOrientations
functions.description: Returns per-block text orientation and vertical writing flags from a prior layout analysis run.
requirements: block_orientation and vertical_writing must be non-null pointers to receive arrays; caller must delete[] the arrays.
Requires previous layout analysis results to exist (e.g., after AnalyseLayout/Recognize).

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetUnichar
functions.description: Returns the UTF-8 string for the specified unichar id from the current UNICHARSET.
requirements: unichar_id must be within the range of the loaded UNICHARSET.
Returned pointer is owned by Tesseract; do not free.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::GetDawg
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the i-th DAWG (dictionary graph) loaded into the engine.
requirements: i must be in [0, NumDawgs()).
Returned pointer is owned by Tesseract; do not delete.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::NumDawgs
functions.description: Returns the number of DAWGs loaded in the engine.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::tesseract
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the underlying Tesseract engine object for advanced/internal use.
requirements: Returned pointer is owned by TessBaseAPI; do not delete.
Internal API; stability not guaranteed across versions.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::oem
functions.description: Returns the last OCR engine mode requested during Init.

functions.name: tesseract::TessBaseAPI::set_min_orientation_margin
functions.description: Sets the minimum orientation margin threshold used internally for orientation decisions.
requirements: margin should be a non-negative double.

functions.name: tesseract::HOcrEscape
functions.description: Escapes an ASCII/UTF-8 string for safe embedding in HTML (hOCR), replacing characters & < > " ' with corresponding HTML entities.
requirements: text must be a valid C-string; may be nullptr only if implementation tolerates it (not specified).
Returned std::string is owned by the caller as a value object.

functions.name: TessVersion
functions.description: Returns a const string with the Tesseract engine version. Useful for logging and diagnostics.
requirements: No arguments required.
Return value is a const pointer owned by the library; do not free it.

functions.name: TessDeleteText
functions.description: Frees a NUL-terminated UTF-8 text buffer returned by certain Tesseract API calls (e.g., TessBaseAPIGetUTF8Text, GetHOCRText, etc.).
requirements: text must be a pointer previously returned by a Tesseract API function that documents freeing via TessDeleteText.
Passing NULL is a no-op (behavior typical but not explicitly stated; if uncertain, pass non-NULL).

functions.name: TessDeleteTextArray
functions.description: Frees an array of C strings (char**) returned by Tesseract APIs that require this deallocator.
requirements: arr must be a pointer previously returned by a Tesseract API function that documents freeing via TessDeleteTextArray.
Assumes the array and its internal strings are freed appropriately by this function (implementation-defined).

functions.name: TessDeleteIntArray
functions.description: Frees an array of ints returned by Tesseract API calls that require this deallocator (e.g., word confidences).
requirements: arr must be a pointer previously returned by a Tesseract API function that documents freeing via TessDeleteIntArray.

functions.name: TessTextRendererCreate
functions.description: Creates a renderer that outputs plain UTF-8 text. Use with TessBaseAPIProcessPage(s) to write OCR results.
requirements: outputbase must be a valid NUL-terminated path/prefix (non-NULL).
Returned pointer must be deleted with TessDeleteResultRenderer.
Renderer may be chained using TessResultRendererInsert.

functions.name: TessHOcrRendererCreate
functions.description: Creates an hOCR renderer (HTML with OCR position data).
requirements: outputbase must be non-NULL and valid.
Delete with TessDeleteResultRenderer.

functions.name: TessHOcrRendererCreate2
functions.description: Creates an hOCR renderer with optional font attribute output.
requirements: outputbase must be non-NULL and valid.
font_info controls inclusion of font attributes (nonzero = enable).
Delete returned renderer with TessDeleteResultRenderer.

functions.name: TessAltoRendererCreate
functions.description: Creates an ALTO XML renderer for OCR results.
requirements: outputbase must be non-NULL and valid.
Delete with TessDeleteResultRenderer.

functions.name: TessPAGERendererCreate
functions.description: Creates a PAGE XML renderer for OCR results.
requirements: outputbase must be non-NULL and valid.
Delete with TessDeleteResultRenderer.

functions.name: TessTsvRendererCreate
functions.description: Creates a TSV renderer (tab-separated values) for OCR results.
requirements: outputbase must be non-NULL and valid.
Delete with TessDeleteResultRenderer.

functions.name: TessPDFRendererCreate
functions.signature: TessResultRenderer *TessPDFRendererCreate(const char *outputbase, const char *datadir, BOOL textonly);
functions.description: Creates a searchable PDF renderer. Uses traineddata resources in datadir. textonly controls text layer only vs embedded images.
requirements: outputbase must be non-NULL and valid.
datadir should point to a valid Tesseract data directory containing language models; behavior undefined otherwise.
textonly nonzero to produce text-only PDF layer.
Delete with TessDeleteResultRenderer.

functions.name: TessUnlvRendererCreate
functions.description: Creates a UNLV format renderer.
requirements: outputbase must be non-NULL and valid.
Delete with TessDeleteResultRenderer.

functions.name: TessBoxTextRendererCreate
functions.description: Creates a .box text renderer for box training data format.
requirements: outputbase must be non-NULL and valid.
Delete with TessDeleteResultRenderer.

functions.name: TessLSTMBoxRendererCreate
functions.description: Creates an LSTM-specific box renderer (for LSTM training data).
requirements: outputbase must be non-NULL and valid.
Delete with TessDeleteResultRenderer.

functions.name: TessWordStrBoxRendererCreate
functions.description: Creates a word/str box renderer for training/analysis.
requirements: outputbase must be non-NULL and valid.
Delete with TessDeleteResultRenderer.

functions.name: TessDeleteResultRenderer
functions.description: Destroys a result renderer and frees its resources.
requirements: renderer must be a renderer created by a Tess*RendererCreate function or part of a chain created likewise.
If renderer is the head of a chain, this typically deletes the chain (implementation-defined). Avoid double-free.

functions.name: TessResultRendererInsert
functions.description: Inserts 'next' after 'renderer' to form a chain of renderers to receive the same OCR results.
requirements: renderer must be a valid, created renderer.
next must be a valid, created renderer not already owned/freed.
Do not insert cycles.

functions.name: TessResultRendererNext
functions.description: Returns the next renderer in the chain, or NULL if none.
requirements: renderer must be a valid renderer pointer.

functions.name: TessResultRendererBeginDocument
functions.description: Begins a multi-page document for the given renderer chain with an optional title.
requirements: renderer must be a valid renderer (head of chain).
Call before adding images; should be paired with TessResultRendererEndDocument.
title may be NULL or a valid UTF-8 string (exact behavior unspecified).
Check return value for success (nonzero).

functions.name: TessResultRendererAddImage
functions.description: Adds the current page/image recognized by 'api' to the renderer chain.
requirements: renderer must be begun with TessResultRendererBeginDocument (typical usage).
api must be a valid TessBaseAPI with an image set and recognition performed as required by the renderer.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: TessResultRendererEndDocument
functions.description: Finalizes the document for the renderer chain, flushing and closing outputs.
requirements: renderer must be a valid renderer for which BeginDocument was called.
Must be called once per begun document.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: TessResultRendererExtention
functions.description: Returns the default file extension for this renderer (e.g., ".txt", ".pdf").
requirements: renderer must be valid.
Returned pointer is owned by library; do not free.

functions.name: TessResultRendererTitle
functions.description: Returns the title associated with the current document for this renderer, if any.
requirements: renderer must be valid.
Returned pointer is owned by library; do not free.

functions.name: TessResultRendererImageNum
functions.description: Returns the number of images/pages processed by this renderer so far.
requirements: renderer must be valid.

functions.name: TessBaseAPICreate
functions.description: Allocates a new TessBaseAPI handle. Must be followed by initialization before recognition operations.
requirements: Delete the handle with TessBaseAPIDelete when done.
Call one of TessBaseAPIInit* before setting images/recognition for most operations.

functions.name: TessBaseAPIDelete
functions.description: Destroys a TessBaseAPI instance and frees associated resources.
requirements: handle must be a pointer previously returned by TessBaseAPICreate.
Do not use the handle after deletion. Avoid double deletion.

functions.name: TessBaseAPISetInputName
functions.description: Sets an input name (typically filename) for metadata and error messages.
requirements: handle must be a valid TessBaseAPI.
name must be a valid UTF-8 string or NULL (behavior for NULL unspecified).

functions.name: TessBaseAPIGetInputName
functions.description: Gets the input name previously set.
requirements: handle must be valid.
Returned pointer may be owned by library; do not free.

functions.name: TessBaseAPISetInputImage
functions.description: Associates a Leptonica Pix as the input image for recognition.
requirements: handle must be valid.
pix must be a valid Pix pointer owned/managed by the caller. The API may copy or reference it (implementation-defined).

functions.name: TessBaseAPIGetInputImage
functions.description: Returns the currently set input Pix image, if any.
requirements: handle must be valid.
Returned Pix pointer ownership is not transferred (do not free unless you own it).

functions.name: TessBaseAPIGetSourceYResolution
functions.description: Returns the Y (vertical) resolution in PPI for the current source image.
requirements: handle must be valid.

functions.name: TessBaseAPIGetDatapath
functions.description: Returns the data path configured for Tesseract (location of traineddata files).
requirements: handle must be valid.
Returned pointer is owned by library; do not free.

functions.name: TessBaseAPISetOutputName
functions.description: Sets the base output name used by certain renderers and outputs.
requirements: handle must be valid.
name must be a valid string (non-NULL recommended).

functions.name: TessBaseAPISetVariable
functions.signature: BOOL TessBaseAPISetVariable(TessBaseAPI *handle, const char *name, const char *value);
functions.description: Sets a configuration variable by name to a string value. Returns nonzero on success.
requirements: handle must be valid.
name and value must be non-NULL valid strings.
Only known variables can be set; check return value.

functions.name: TessBaseAPISetDebugVariable
functions.signature: BOOL TessBaseAPISetDebugVariable(TessBaseAPI *handle, const char *name, const char *value);
functions.description: Sets a debug-only configuration variable. Returns nonzero on success.
requirements: handle must be valid.
name and value must be non-NULL strings.
Only debug variables are accepted; check return value.

functions.name: TessBaseAPIGetIntVariable
functions.signature: BOOL TessBaseAPIGetIntVariable(const TessBaseAPI *handle, const char *name, int *value);
functions.description: Gets an integer config variable by name into value. Returns nonzero on success.
requirements: handle must be valid.
name must be non-NULL.
value must be a non-NULL pointer to int for output.
Check return value before using *value.

functions.name: TessBaseAPIGetBoolVariable
functions.signature: BOOL TessBaseAPIGetBoolVariable(const TessBaseAPI *handle, const char *name, BOOL *value);
functions.description: Gets a boolean config variable by name. Returns nonzero on success.
requirements: handle must be valid.
name must be non-NULL.
value must be non-NULL.
Check return value before using *value.

functions.name: TessBaseAPIGetDoubleVariable
functions.signature: BOOL TessBaseAPIGetDoubleVariable(const TessBaseAPI *handle, const char *name, double *value);
functions.description: Gets a double config variable by name. Returns nonzero on success.
requirements: handle must be valid.
name must be non-NULL.
value must be non-NULL.
Check return value before using *value.

functions.name: TessBaseAPIGetStringVariable
functions.description: Gets a string config variable by name. Returns a const pointer.
requirements: handle must be valid.
name must be non-NULL.
Returned pointer is owned by library; do not free.

functions.name: TessBaseAPIPrintVariables
functions.description: Prints current variables and values to the given FILE stream.
requirements: handle must be valid.
fp must be a valid FILE* opened for writing.

functions.name: TessBaseAPIPrintVariablesToFile
functions.description: Writes current variables and values to a file by name.
requirements: handle must be valid.
filename must be a valid non-NULL path.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: TessBaseAPIInit1

functions.description: Initializes the OCR engine with datapath, language(s), engine mode, and a list of config files.

datapath may be NULL to use defaults or a valid path.
language is a language string (e.g., "eng" or "eng+deu").
configs is an array of char* of length configs_size (may be NULL if size is 0).
Returns 0 on success, nonzero on failure (conventional for Tesseract).

functions.name: TessBaseAPIInit2
functions.signature: int TessBaseAPIInit2(TessBaseAPI *handle, const char *datapath, const char *language, TessOcrEngineMode oem);
functions.description: Initializes the OCR engine with datapath, language(s), and engine mode.
requirements: handle must be valid and not already initialized (or properly ended).
datapath may be NULL or valid path.
language string must be valid.
Check return value.

functions.name: TessBaseAPIInit3
functions.signature: int TessBaseAPIInit3(TessBaseAPI *handle, const char *datapath, const char *language);
functions.description: Initializes the OCR engine with datapath and language(s), using default engine mode.
requirements: handle must be valid.
datapath may be NULL or valid path.
language must be valid.
Check return value.

functions.name: TessBaseAPIInit4
functions.signature: int TessBaseAPIInit4(TessBaseAPI *handle, const char *datapath, const char *language, TessOcrEngineMode mode, char **configs, int configs_size, char **vars_vec, char **vars_values, size_t vars_vec_size, BOOL set_only_non_debug_params);

datapath/language as above.
configs is an array of length configs_size (may be NULL if size 0).
vars_vec and vars_values are arrays of length vars_vec_size containing paired names and values (may be NULL if size 0).
set_only_non_debug_params nonzero to restrict variable setting.
Check return value.

requirements: handle must be valid.
data must point to a buffer of size data_size containing appropriate data resources.
language/mode/configs/vars parameters as in Init4.
Check return value.

functions.name: TessBaseAPIGetInitLanguagesAsString
functions.description: Returns the languages used in the last successful initialization as a string.

Returned pointer is owned by library; do not free.

functions.name: TessBaseAPIGetLoadedLanguagesAsVector
functions.description: Returns a NULL-terminated vector of language codes currently loaded.

functions.name: TessBaseAPIGetAvailableLanguagesAsVector
functions.description: Returns a NULL-terminated vector of language codes available in the datapath.
requirements: handle must be valid.
Caller must free with TessDeleteTextArray (inferred).

functions.name: TessBaseAPIInitForAnalysePage
functions.description: Initializes internal data structures for page layout analysis without performing full recognition.

functions.name: TessBaseAPIReadConfigFile
functions.description: Applies configuration parameters from a config file.
requirements: handle must be valid.
filename must refer to an accessible config file.
Call before recognition to take effect.

functions.name: TessBaseAPIReadDebugConfigFile
functions.description: Applies debug configuration parameters from a config file.
requirements: handle must be valid.
filename must be accessible.
Use for debug params.

functions.name: TessBaseAPISetPageSegMode
functions.description: Sets the page segmentation mode (PSM) for recognition.

functions.name: TessBaseAPIGetPageSegMode
functions.description: Gets the current page segmentation mode.
requirements: handle must be valid.

functions.name: TessBaseAPIClearAdaptiveClassifier

functions.name: TessBaseAPISetImage2
functions.description: Sets the image to be recognized from a Leptonica Pix.

pix must be a valid Pix pointer.

functions.name: TessBaseAPISetSourceResolution
functions.description: Sets the source image resolution in pixels per inch (PPI).

functions.name: TessBaseAPIGetGradient
functions.description: Returns a gradient metric for the current image/page (exact semantics not documented here).

pixa may be NULL or a non-NULL output parameter to receive a Pixa* array of images.

import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# We need to generate valid UTF-8 text buffers suitable for various Tesseract fuzz stubs.
# Strategy: compose mostly-valid UTF-8 covering ASCII, multi-byte codepoints, separators,
# path-like strings, and variable-like name=value pairs. Limit size <= 4096 bytes.

ASCII_LETTERS = string.ascii_letters
ASCII_DIGITS = string.digits
ASCII_SAFE = ASCII_LETTERS + ASCII_DIGITS + "_-"
PATH_SEP_CANDIDATES = ["/", "\\"]

# Some Unicode ranges for valid UTF-8 code points (exclude surrogates and common noncharacters)
UNICODE_RANGES: List[Tuple[int, int]] = [
    (0x0020, 0x007E),   # Printable ASCII
    (0x00A0, 0x024F),   # Latin-1 Supplement + Latin Extended
    (0x0370, 0x03FF),   # Greek
    (0x0400, 0x04FF),   # Cyrillic
    (0x0590, 0x05FF),   # Hebrew
    (0x0600, 0x06FF),   # Arabic
    (0x0900, 0x097F),   # Devanagari
    (0x3040, 0x309F),   # Hiragana
    (0x30A0, 0x30FF),   # Katakana
    (0x4E00, 0x9FFF),   # CJK Unified Ideographs
    (0x1F300, 0x1F64F), # Misc symbols and emoticons
]

COMBINING_CHARS = [0x0301, 0x0300, 0x0302, 0x0308, 0x0327, 0x0323, 0x0304, 0x0307]

def rnd(r: random.Random, a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return r.randint(a, b)

def pick_codepoint(r: random.Random) -> int:
    # Choose from predefined ranges, avoid surrogates/noncharacters
    rng = r.choice(UNICODE_RANGES)
    cp = rnd(r, rng[0], rng[1])
    # Avoid surrogates explicitly
    if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
        cp = 0x20
    # Avoid common noncharacters (..FFFE/..FFFF)
    if (cp & 0xFFFE) == 0xFFFE:
        cp = 0x20
    return cp

def encode_cp(cp: int) -> str:
    return chr(cp)

def make_ascii_token(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rnd(r, min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(r.choice(ASCII_SAFE) for _ in range(n))

def make_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build a simple path with 1-3 segments, including an extension sometimes
    segs = []
    for _ in range(rnd(r, 1, 3)):
        seg = make_ascii_token(r, 1, rnd(r, 3, 10))
        segs.append(seg)
    ext = ''
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        ext = '.' + r.choice(['txt', 'png', 'jpg', 'tif', 'tiff', 'pdf', 'cfg', 'ini'])
    sep = r.choice(PATH_SEP_CANDIDATES)
    path = sep.join(segs) + ext
    # Prepend root sometimes
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        path = sep + path
    return path

def make_mixed_text(r: random.Random, words: int) -> str:
    parts = []
    for _ in range(words):
        if r.random() < 0.6:
            base = make_ascii_token(r, 2, 8)
            if r.random() < 0.5:
                base += ''.join(encode_cp(r.choice(COMBINING_CHARS)) for _ in range(rnd(r, 1, 3)))
            parts.append(base)
        else:
            ncp = rnd(r, 1, 6)
            s = ''.join(encode_cp(pick_codepoint(r)) for _ in range(ncp))
            parts.append(s)
    punct = [',', '.', ';', ':', ' — ', ' – ']
    out = ''
    for i, w in enumerate(parts):
        if i:
            out += r.choice([' ', ' ', ' ', '\n', '\t', '  '])
        out += w
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            out += r.choice(punct)
    return out

def make_utf8_samples(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Include 1/2/3/4-byte UTF-8 codepoints
    samples = [
        0x0041,       # 'A' (1 byte)
        0x00E9,       # 'é' (2 bytes)
        0x20AC,       # Euro (3 bytes)
        0x10348,      # Gothic letter (4 bytes)
        0x05D0,       # Hebrew Alef
        0x0627,       # Arabic Alef
        0x0905,       # Devanagari A
        0x4E2D,       # CJK
        0x1F600,      # 😀
    ]
    r.shuffle(samples)
    return ''.join(encode_cp(cp) for cp in samples)

def make_separators(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Provide common separators and paragraph/line separators
    candidates = ["\n", "\r\n", "\n\n", "\t", " | ", "\u2029", "\u2028"]
    # Turn unicode escape strings into actual characters for U+2029/U+2028
    normalized = []
    for c in candidates:
        if c.startswith("\\u"):
            code = int(c[2:], 16)
            normalized.append(chr(code))
        else:
            normalized.append(c)
    return r.choice(normalized) * rnd(r, 1, 3)

def assemble_payload(r: random.Random, target_size: int) -> str:
    parts: List[str] = []

    # 1) Variable-like tokens with values
    for _ in range(rnd(r, 2, 5)):
        key = make_ascii_token(r, 3, 12)
        val_type = r.random()
        if val_type < 0.4:
            val = make_ascii_token(r, 1, 8)
        elif val_type < 0.7:
            val = str(rnd(r, 0, 1000))
        else:
            val = r.choice(["true", "false", "1", "0", "yes", "no"])
        parts.append(f"{key}={val}")

    # 2) Filename/path hint
    parts.append(make_path(r))

    # 3) Mixed multilingual text
    parts.append(make_mixed_text(r, rnd(r, 5, 20)))

    # 4) Separator candidates
    parts.append(make_separators(r))

    # 5) UTF-8 sample set
    parts.append(make_utf8_samples(r))

    # 6) Short paragraph-like blocks
    for _ in range(rnd(r, 1, 3)):
        parts.append(make_mixed_text(r, rnd(r, 5, 12)))
        parts.append("\n")

    # 7) Extra single codepoints to exercise iterator stepping
    extra = ''.join(encode_cp(pick_codepoint(r)) for _ in range(rnd(r, 5, 20)))
    parts.append(extra)

    text = '\n'.join(parts)
    # Trim to target size by code point to avoid splitting UTF-8 sequences
    enc = text.encode('utf-8')
    if len(enc) > target_size:
        acc_chars = []
        total = 0
        for ch in text:
            b = ch.encode('utf-8')
            if total + len(b) > target_size:
                break
            acc_chars.append(ch)
            total += len(b)
        text = ''.join(acc_chars)
    return text


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Target around 1024-2048 bytes to give rich content but keep under 4096
    target = r.randint(800, 2000)
    s = assemble_payload(r, target)
    if not s:
        s = "Hello\n"
    if r.random() < 0.5 and not s.endswith('\n'):
        s += "\n"
    data = s.encode('utf-8')
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: filesystem path string
# Fuzzer uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR to supply:
# - output base for various Tess*Renderer constructors (text, tsv, alto, page, pdf, unlv, lstmbox, boxtext, wordstrbox)
# - SetOutputName on TessBaseAPI
# - PDF renderer additionally requests a datadir string via FUZZ_PARAM_STR
#
# Valid, interesting inputs should therefore be plausible filesystem path/base names:
# - Short and long (but <= 64 for base, <= 128 for datadir per stub) names
# - With/without directories
# - With different extensions
# - Including characters often used in file paths: '-', '_', '.', spaces
# - Relative paths ("./", "../") and nested directories
# - Absolute style paths (both POSIX "/tmp/..." and Windows-like "C:\\...")
# - Unicode in UTF-8 (since Tesseract is UTF-8 friendly)
# - Names likely to trigger different file-extension logic in renderers (though renderers mostly add their own ext)
#
# The fuzzer framework will consume a single bytes buffer and split it into FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
# in order. We therefore encode multiple strings in one buffer, separated by newlines. If fewer
# are needed, extras are ignored; if more are needed, some strings may be reused by the harness,
# but providing a variety helps exploration.
#
# We generate a sequence:
#   1) A general output base (<=64 bytes)
#   2) Another variant output base (<=64 bytes)
#   3) A plausible datadir path (<=128 bytes)
#   4) Additional assorted path strings to be consumed by other FUZZ_PARAM_STR sites.
#
# All strings are valid UTF-8 and kept <= 256 bytes; whole buffer <= 4096 bytes.

POSIX_SEPS = "/"
WIN_SEP = "\\"

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ ."

UNICODE_PIECES = [
    "Δ", "漢字", "русский", "árbol", "ファイル", "파일", "😀", "½", "ç", "ß"
]

EXTS = [
    "", "txt", "hocr", "alto", "xml", "tsv", "pdf", "box", "lstmf", "dat"
]

DRIVES = [
    "C:", "D:", "E:", "Z:"  # Windows-like
]

def rand_name(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 32, allow_ext: bool = True) -> str:
    # Build a base name with safe chars and occasional unicode
    parts: List[str] = []
    length = rng.randint(1, max_len)
    while len("".join(parts)) < length:
        if rng.random() < 0.15:
            parts.append(rng.choice(UNICODE_PIECES))
        else:
            run = rng.randint(1, 6)
            parts.append("".join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(run)))
    base = "".join(parts).strip()
    base = base.replace("..", ".")  # avoid parent traversal getting collapsed accidentally
    base = base.strip() or "out"
    # Optionally append an extension
    if allow_ext and rng.random() < 0.6:
        ext = rng.choice(EXTS)
        if ext:
            base = base.rstrip(".")
            base = base[: max(1, max_len - len(ext) - 1)]
            base += "." + ext
    # Ensure not too long
    return base[:max_len]

def posix_path(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    depth = rng.randint(0, 4)
    comps = []
    for _ in range(depth):
        comps.append(rand_name(rng, max_len=min(16, max_len // max(1, depth)), allow_ext=False))
    leaf = rand_name(rng, max_len=min(32, max_len // 2), allow_ext=True)
    path = POSIX_SEPS.join([c for c in comps if c])
    if path:
        path = path + "/" + leaf
    else:
        path = leaf
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        path = "./" + path
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        path = "../" + path
    if rng.random() < 0.1:
        path = "/" + path.lstrip("/")
    return path[:max_len]

def win_path(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    drive = rng.choice(DRIVES)
    depth = rng.randint(0, 4)
    comps = []
    for _ in range(depth):
        comps.append(rand_name(rng, max_len=min(16, max_len // max(1, depth)), allow_ext=False))
    leaf = rand_name(rng, max_len=min(32, max_len // 2), allow_ext=True)
    path = drive + WIN_SEP + WIN_SEP.join([c for c in comps if c] + [leaf])
    # Occasionally use mixed separators as many libs accept both
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        path = path.replace(WIN_SEP, POSIX_SEPS, rng.randint(1, 3))
    return path[:max_len]

def ensure_max_bytes(s: str, limit: int) -> str:
    # Trim by bytes (UTF-8 safe)
    b = s.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) <= limit:
        return s
    # Cut to limit, then backtrack to a valid boundary
    b = b[:limit]
    while True:
        try:
            return b.decode('utf-8')
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            b = b[:-1]

def build_strings(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    out: List[str] = []

    # Primary output base candidates (<=64 bytes)
    for _ in range(3):
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            s = posix_path(rng, 48)
        else:
            s = rand_name(rng, 48, allow_ext=True)
        out.append(ensure_max_bytes(s, 64) or "out")

    # PDF datadir style paths (<=128 bytes)
    for _ in range(2):
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            s = posix_path(rng, 110)
        else:
            s = win_path(rng, 110)
        out.append(ensure_max_bytes(s, 128) or ".")

    # Additional assorted bases for chain insertions
    for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 12)):
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.3:
            s = rand_name(rng, 40, allow_ext=True)
        elif choice < 0.6:
            s = posix_path(rng, 60)
        else:
            s = win_path(rng, 60)
        out.append(ensure_max_bytes(s, 128))

    # Include some minimal and edge-case strings
    out.extend([
        "out",  # default fallback used by stubs
        ".",   # current directory
        "..",  # parent directory
        "./out-base", 
        "../rel/dir/output",
        "/tmp/tess/out",
        "C:\\temp\\tess\\out",
        "名/出力/基底",
        "δεδομένα/έξοδος",
    ])

    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq: List[str] = []
    for s in out:
        if s not in seen and s != "":
            seen.add(s)
            uniq.append(s)

    return uniq


def pack_lines(strs: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join with newlines, ensure <= 4096 bytes
    data = "\n".join(strs).encode('utf-8')
    if len(data) <= 4096:
        return data
    # Trim conservatively by reducing number of lines
    b = bytearray()
    for s in strs:
        line = (s + "\n").encode('utf-8')
        if len(b) + len(line) > 4096:
            break
        b.extend(line)
    return bytes(b)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    strs = build_strings(rng)
    return pack_lines(strs)

# This generator produces file contents for fuzz stubs that request FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
# The target API (Tesseract) may read these files as:
# - datapath, language/config files
# - image filenames for ProcessPages
# - renderer output bases (generally path strings; may create files)
# - PrintVariables destinations (opened writable)
# We must provide bytes that are valid for multiple plausible consumers:
# 1) Small valid raster images (PNG) for filename inputs used as images.
# 2) Tesseract config-like text for ReadConfigFile / ReadDebugConfigFile.
# 3) Datapath-like directory tarball is not expected; but plain file is OK. Keep harmless.

# - Tiny grayscale PNGs containing text-like pixels to exercise OCR quickly.

# ---------------- PNG utilities ----------------

def _crc32(data: bytes) -> int:
    # Standard CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3) used by PNG
    return (0xFFFFFFFF & (import_zlib().crc32(data)))

_z = None

def import_zlib():
    global _z
    if _z is None:
        import zlib as _zlib
        _z = _zlib
    return _z


def _png_chunk(typ: bytes, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    import_zlib()
    length = struct.pack('>I', len(payload))
    chunk = typ + payload
    crc = import_zlib().crc32(chunk) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    return length + chunk + struct.pack('>I', crc)


def _make_png(width: int, height: int, color_type: int, bit_depth: int, pixels: bytes, interlace: int = 0) -> bytes:
    # color_type: 0=grayscale,2=truecolor,3=indexed,4=gray+alpha,6=rgba
    # bit_depth typical: 8
    import_zlib()
    sig = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
    ihdr = struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', width, height, bit_depth, color_type, 0, 0, interlace)
    ihdr_chunk = _png_chunk(b'IHDR', ihdr)
    idat_chunk = _png_chunk(b'IDAT', import_zlib().compress(pixels, level=9))
    iend_chunk = _png_chunk(b'IEND', b'')
    return sig + ihdr_chunk + idat_chunk + iend_chunk


def _filter_none_scanlines(raw_rows: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Prepend 0 filter byte per row
    return b''.join(b'\x00' + row for row in raw_rows)


def _gen_png_textlike(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Small grayscale image with simple glyph-like patterns to be quick to OCR.
    w = rng.choice([16, 24, 32])

    color_type = 0  # grayscale
    # Build rows with dark on light stripes forming ASCII-like bars.
    rows = []
    for y in range(h):

        for x in range(w):
            # Create alternating vertical bars and a midline
            val = 240
            if (x // 2) % 2 == 0:

            if y in (h//2, h//2 - 1):
                val = 10
            # sprinkle a simple diagonal
            if (x - y) % 7 == 0:
                val = 200
            row[x] = val
        rows.append(bytes(row))
    pixels = _filter_none_scanlines(rows)
    return _make_png(w, h, color_type, bit_depth, pixels)


def _gen_png_random(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Generate small valid PNG in different color formats.
    w = rng.randint(8, 64)
    h = rng.randint(8, 64)
    bit_depth = 8
    color_type = rng.choice([0, 2, 6])  # grayscale, RGB, RGBA

    elif color_type == 2:

    rows = []
    for _ in range(h):
